question: A meeting of the legislature is usually brought to an end with __________
solution: A meeting or session of the legislature is brought to an end by prorogation. Prorogation closes a parliamentary session, and members go on break until the next session is opened. An adjournment only stops a sitting for a short while, while a dissolution ends the whole parliament before a new election.

question: The charter of the United Nations was drawn up in ________
solution: The Charter of the United Nations was drawn up at a conference in San Francisco in 1945, where representatives of about fifty nations met and signed it. That is why San Francisco is remembered as the birthplace of the UN Charter. New York, Washington DC and Los Angeles were not the meeting place.

question: Nigeria's non-aligned policy means that she will _________

option.a: have nothing to do with the superpowers
option.b: not take sides in international issues based on ideological considerations
option.c: avoid having any dealing with any country with ideological learnings
option.d: relate only with member countries of the Non-Aligned movement

solution: Non-alignment means that Nigeria does not join any of the big power blocs or take sides in their quarrels simply because of ideology. Nigeria decides each international issue on its own merit. It does not mean refusing to deal with the superpowers, and it does not mean relating only to members of the Non-Aligned Movement.

question: The founder of the Universal Negro Improvement Association was ________
solution: The Universal Negro Improvement Association (UNIA) was founded by Marcus Garvey, a Jamaican who encouraged black people everywhere to be proud of themselves and to unite. Herbert Macaulay was a Nigerian nationalist, W. E. B. DuBois was an American scholar, and Casey Hayford was a Ghanaian nationalist, but none of them founded the UNIA.

question: The Premier of Western Region immediately after independence was _________
solution: Immediately after independence in 1960, Chief Ladoke Akintola was the Premier of the Western Region. Chief Obafemi Awolowo had been Premier before independence but left to become Leader of the Opposition at the federal level. Dr. M. A. Majekodunmi was an administrator, and Alhaji D. S. Adegbenro later acted in the region.
category: Institutions of Government in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: A constitution is a legal document _________

option.c: forming the basis upon which a government rules the country
option.d: only likely to succeed in countries where there is union government

solution: A constitution is the body of fundamental rules and principles that shows how a country is governed and forms the basis on which a government rules. It is not merely a document drawn up by lawyers, and it is not only military decrees. A country can succeed with a constitution even if it does not practise a unitary system.

question: The economic basis of feudalism is __________
solution: The economic basis of feudalism is agriculture. In a feudal system, land was the most important form of wealth, and lords owned large farms worked by peasants who depended on them. Capital, trade and slavery were important in other systems, but land and farming were the foundation of feudalism.

question: The application of the rule of law may be constrained by ________

option.a: securing the tenure of office of judges
option.c: employing men of proven integrity as judges

solution: The rule of law can be limited when a government invokes emergency powers during a crisis such as war or serious unrest. In an emergency, rights may be restricted and special laws may be used. Securing judges' tenure, keeping judges away from partisan politics and appointing honest judges all strengthen the rule of law instead of limiting it.

question: In a democracy, sovereignty is in _________
solution: In a democracy, sovereignty belongs to the people — that is, to the community of citizens. The people choose their leaders and can remove them through elections. Public officials, judges and the Head of State only exercise power on behalf of the people; the power does not belong to them personally.

question: The delineation of constituencies is a major duty of the __________
solution: The electoral commission is the body that delineates (marks out) constituencies so that elections can be organised fairly. In Nigeria this work is done by the electoral body (now INEC), often with the help of the Boundary Commission. The National Assembly and political parties do not draw constituency boundaries.

question: A characteristic feature of communism is __________
solution: A key feature of communism is dictatorship — rule by one party that does not allow rival parties to compete for power. Free enterprise, liberal democracy and a multi-party system belong to capitalist or democratic systems, not to communism.

question: Within the United Nations, the vote power is exercised in __________
solution: The real veto power in the United Nations is exercised in the Security Council. Its five permanent members — the United States, Britain, France, Russia and China — can each block a decision with a single “no” vote. The General Assembly, UNESCO and WHO do not have this veto power.

question: Rates are generally collected in Nigeria by ________
solution: Rates (property rates) are collected by the Local Government Council. Local governments are allowed to raise money through rates, market and motor-park fees, and licences. State ministries of finance and the inland revenue department handle other taxes, not local rates.

question: A set of internalized norms which guides political action is called ________
solution: A set of internalised norms that guides political action is called a value. Values are the beliefs a society holds about what is right, fair and important, and they quietly shape how people take part in politics. Power is the ability to make others obey, law is a written rule, and a symbol is a sign such as a flag.

question: Which of the following was the last to win independence from colonial rule ?
solution: Among the countries listed, Angola was the last to win independence from colonial rule, gaining it from Portugal in 1975. Côte d'Ivoire became independent in 1960, Algeria in 1962, and Tanzania (Tanganyika) in 1961. Portugal held on to its African colonies longer than Britain and France did.

question: Warrant Chiefs were appointed to __________
solution: The British appointed Warrant Chiefs to take charge of local administration in areas where there were no traditional rulers, especially in Eastern Nigeria. The chiefs collected taxes and kept order for the colonial government. They were not appointed to prevent tribal wars, supervise native courts or decide divorce cases.

question: NEPAD was adopted during the OAU summit held in _________
solution: NEPAD (the New Partnership for Africa's Development) was adopted at the OAU summit held in Lusaka, Zambia, in 2001. It was created to help African countries plan their own development, reduce poverty and attract support. Tunis, Cairo and Abuja hosted other meetings, not the NEPAD summit.

question: A feature unique to General Murtala Muhammed's Supreme Military Council as compared to that of General Yakubu Gowon was the _________

option.a: inclusion of the civilians as members
option.b: exclusion of military governors from the council
option.c: inclusion of the chief justice as a member
option.d: the exclusion of the Inspector General of police from the council

solution: The unique feature of General Murtala Muhammed's Supreme Military Council was that it excluded military governors from the council. Murtala wanted decision-making to be more central and faster. Civilian members, the Chief Justice and the Inspector-General of Police were not the special change compared with Gowon's council.

question: Which of the following was not established by the 1979 Nigerian constitution?
solution: The National Universities Commission (NUC) was not established by the 1979 Constitution. The constitution provided for bodies such as the Police Service Commission, the Federal Electoral Commission and the National Population Commission. The NUC was created by an ordinary law to regulate universities.

question: The simple plurality electoral system is often criticized because _________

option.a: the ruling party may lose the election
option.b: the winner may not poll an absolute majority
option.c: it works against all opposition parties

solution: The simple plurality (first-past-the-post) system is criticised because the winner may not poll an absolute majority of the votes. A candidate can win with, say, 40% when the other votes are shared among several rivals. It is not criticised because the ruling party may lose, and rigging is not a special feature of this system.

question: Africans were first elected to the legislative council in British West Africa in _________
solution: Africans were first elected to a legislative council in British West Africa in Nigeria, under the Clifford Constitution of 1922. Four elected members were allowed — three for Lagos and one for Calabar. Ghana, Sierra Leone and The Gambia did not have elected African members before that.

question: A condition for judicial independence is the appointment of judges by the __________
solution: Judicial independence is protected when judges are appointed on the advice of the Judicial Service Commission rather than by politicians. The commission recommends qualified and honest lawyers for appointment, so judges do not owe their jobs to the government of the day. The Civil Service, Law Review Commission and Code of Conduct Bureau do not appoint judges.

question: A bill that applies to the whole population and is intended to promote the general welfare is called _________
solution: A public bill is a bill that applies to the whole population and is meant to promote the general welfare, such as a bill on health or education. A private bill affects only a particular person or group, while a decree is a law made by a military government. “Appropriate bill” is not a standard term.

question: Which of the following is a good example of a confederal state?
solution: Switzerland is the best example of a confederal state among the options. In a confederation, the member states keep most of their power and give only limited authority to the centre. Nigeria and the USA operate federal systems, while ECOWAS is a regional organisation of states, not a single state.

question: While pressure groups aim at influencing government decisions, the primary aim of political parties is to ______

option.a: promote the welfare of their members
option.c: influence legislation in order to benefit their members

solution: The primary aim of a political party is to control political power by winning elections and forming the government. Pressure groups only try to influence government decisions. Promoting members' welfare and influencing legislation are secondary activities, not the main goal of a party.

question: The theory of separation of powers was first time clearly formulated by __________
solution: The theory of separation of powers was clearly formulated by Baron de Montesquieu, a French thinker, in his book The Spirit of the Laws. He argued that the legislature, executive and judiciary should be separate so that no one arm becomes too powerful. Jean Bodin, John Austin and Lord Bryce wrote about other ideas.

question: The Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy in the 1979 constitution do not include _________

option.c: concentration of wealth and provision of maximum welfare

solution: The Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy in the 1979 Constitution did not include “national integration and ethnic loyalty”. The constitution promoted national integration and loyalty to the nation, not loyalty to ethnic groups. Democracy, social justice, federal character and maximum welfare were part of the objectives.

question: The Gulf War of 1990 is an indication that the U. N. O. is unable to _______
solution: The 1990 Gulf War showed that the UNO could not ensure permanent world peace. The UN was set up to keep peace, yet a major war still broke out. The war did not show a failure to promote world trade, stop colonialism or control armament, even though those are also UN concerns.

question: The judicial organ of government is the body which _________
solution: The judiciary is the organ of government that interprets the law. It explains what the law means and decides cases in court. Making laws is the work of the legislature, while implementing laws and punishing lawbreakers is the work of the executive and its agencies.

question: In the First Republic, Nigeria was very reluctant to have meaningful interaction with ________
solution: In the First Republic, Nigeria was very reluctant to interact meaningfully with the Soviet Union. The Western-leaning government was suspicious of communism during the Cold War. Italy, the United States and Germany were not treated with the same distance.

question: Southern Nigeria was divided into Eastern and Western provinces for administrative purposes in _________
solution: Southern Nigeria was divided into the Eastern and Western Provinces in 1939 for administrative convenience. The British did this to make the large southern territory easier to govern. The years 1935, 1937 and 1941 are incorrect.

question: The British Government revoked the charter of the Royal Niger Company and took over the direct administration of Nigeria in _________
solution: In 1900 the British government revoked the charter of the Royal Niger Company and took direct control of Nigeria. The company had ruled parts of the north and south on behalf of Britain, but the government then set up direct colonial administration. 1861, 1906 and 1914 are other important dates in colonial history, not the year of the revocation.

question: A government in which control of ultimate power is by a few who rule in their selfish interest is classified as _________
solution: A government in which ultimate power is controlled by a few people who rule in their own selfish interest is an oligarchy. A dictatorship is rule by one person, an aristocracy is rule by the “best” or noble class, and a monarchy is rule by a king or queen.

question: A system of government in which power derives from total control of the instruments of force is called ___________
solution: A system in which power comes from total control of the instruments of force is fascism. Fascist leaders use the army, police and propaganda to crush opposition and control every part of life. Monarchy, oligarchy and capitalism do not depend mainly on force in this way.

question: When a state is subject to no other authority, it is said to be _________
solution: A state that is subject to no other authority is sovereign. Sovereignty means supreme power within a territory and freedom from outside control. A state may be powerful, legitimate or authoritative without being completely free from the control of another state.

question: Fascism developed in________
solution: Fascism developed in Italy under Benito Mussolini from 1922. He built a one-party state that glorified the nation and used force against opponents. France, Germany and China had other political experiences; Nazism, a related ideology, grew in Germany.

question: In the traditional Hausa-Fulani political system, political authority was vested in the ___________
solution: In the traditional Hausa-Fulani political system, political authority was vested in the Emir. The Emir ruled the emirate with the help of officials and an Emirate Council, but final authority rested with him. The Talakawa were the common people, and the Alkali was a judge.

question: The highest court in Nigeria before 1963 was the _________

option.c: Judicial Committees of the Privy Council

solution: Before Nigeria became a republic in 1963, the highest court of appeal was the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London. Appeals from Nigerian courts could go there. After 1963, the Supreme Court of Nigeria became the final court.
category: Institutions of Government in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: Which of the following is not associated with local government elections?
solution: Constituency is not associated with local government elections in the same way as the others. Local government elections are organised by wards, using ballot boxes and electoral officers. A constituency is mainly used for state and federal elections.

question: The idea of making the civil service permanent, neutral and anonymous is to _________

option.a: make civil servants a functional elite

solution: Making the civil service permanent, neutral and anonymous is meant to enhance efficiency in administration. Officials keep their jobs when governments change, serve any ruling party loyally, and give advice without seeking public credit. This gives the country stable and experienced administration.

question: The ....... is responsible for advising the president of Nigeria on the sovereignty and territorial Integrity of the country.
solution: The National Defence Council advises the President on matters concerning the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Nigeria, including the defence of the country. The Council of State advises on general policy, the National Security Council handles security intelligence, and the Federal Executive Council advises on day-to-day governance.
category: Institutions of Government in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: Nigeria's withdrawal from the Edinburg Commonwealth Games in July 1986 was in protest against British.....

option.a: Failure to impose sanctions on South Africa

solution: Nigeria withdrew from the Edinburgh Commonwealth Games in 1986 to protest Britain's failure to impose sanctions on South Africa over apartheid. Nigeria believed Britain was not doing enough to pressure the racist South African government. The protest was not about rude remarks, arms to Rhodesia or Angola.

question: When Nigeria achieved independence in 1960, the head of state was the _____
solution: When Nigeria became independent on 1 October 1960, the Head of State was the Queen of England, represented in Nigeria by a Governor-General. Nigeria was still a constitutional monarchy and only became a republic in 1963, when a Nigerian President replaced the Queen. The Prime Minister was the Head of Government.

question: The Economic Community of West African States has made progress in the area of ....

option.d: Free movement of persons and right of residence

solution: ECOWAS has recorded its clearest progress in the free movement of persons and the right of residence among member states. Citizens of member countries can travel, live and work in one another's countries under the ECOWAS protocol. Trade has grown, but providing financial aid and achieving political integration have been much slower.

question: ________refers to the manipulation of boundaries of constituencies in order to win more seats,
solution: Gerrymandering is the manipulation of constituency boundaries to favour a particular party or candidate. It is done by drawing boundaries in a way that packs opponents together or spreads them out. Delimitation is the normal, fair marking of boundaries, while devolution means transferring power to lower levels of government.

question: A major issue that distinguishes pressure groups from political parties is the ...
solution: The major difference between pressure groups and political parties is their objective. Political parties want to win elections and control government, while pressure groups only try to influence government policy. Both may have members and ideologies, so membership and voting pattern do not separate them clearly.

question: Financial allocation to local governments by the federal or the state government to supplement the cost of a project is called_____
solution: A matching grant is money given to a local government by the federal or state government to help pay for a project, usually on condition that the local government also contributes its own share. Revenue allocation is the general sharing of national income, while statutory allocation is the regular share given by law.

question: The type of government operated in Nigeria between October 1st 1979 to December 3 1983 is called a __________
solution: Nigeria operated a presidential system of government from 1 October 1979 to 31 December 1983 under President Shehu Shagari. In that system, the President was both Head of State and Head of Government and was elected directly by the people. The parliamentary system had been used in the First Republic.

question: The Nigeria's head of government in 1963 was _____
solution: In 1963, Nigeria's Head of Government was Alhaji Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, who was the Prime Minister. Chief Nnamdi Azikiwe was the ceremonial President and Head of State. General Gowon and Major-General Ironsi came later through military rule.
category: Institutions of Government in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: During the Civil War, the major power that expressed moral support for Biafra's self- determination was ......
solution: During the Nigerian Civil War, France was the major power that expressed moral and some material support for Biafra's claim to self-determination. Britain and the United States supported the Federal Government, while China also backed the Federal side. France's support encouraged the Biafran leadership to continue the war.

question: One of the duties of the legislature is to_______
solution: One of the duties of the legislature is to exercise oversight over the executive — checking how laws are implemented and how public money is spent. Implementing laws is the work of the executive, promulgating decrees is done by military governments, and adjudicating disputes belongs to the judiciary.

question: The Barclay's Bank and the British Petroleum Company in Nigeria were nationalized in the late 1970s for transacting business with ...
solution: Barclays Bank and British Petroleum were nationalised in Nigeria in the late 1970s because they were transacting business with South Africa during the apartheid era. Nigeria opposed apartheid and wanted to punish companies that supported the racist regime. The companies were not nationalised over dealings with Libya, France or Portugal.

question: ____________was the method used by the British to facilitate the administration of Southern Nigeria.
solution: The British used divide and rule to make the administration of Southern Nigeria easier. They encouraged differences between groups and dealt with communities separately so that no united opposition could form against colonial rule. Trade associations, dialogue and persuasion were not the main administrative method.

question: Which of the following is a founding member of OPEC?
solution: Venezuela was a founding member of OPEC at the Baghdad Conference in 1960. The founding members were Venezuela, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq and Kuwait. Indonesia, Algeria and Nigeria joined OPEC later, so they were not founding members.

question: The Native Authority System was most effective and successful in .......
solution: The Native Authority System was most effective and successful in Northern Nigeria. The emirs already had strong, centralised traditional authority, so the British found it easy to rule through them. The system worked less smoothly in the south, where political authority was more dispersed.

question: The major problem of the ECOWAS is lack of _______
solution: The major problem of ECOWAS is the lack of commitment by members. Member states often put their own national interests first and fail to implement agreed decisions, which slows down integration. Lack of a uniform ideology or common currency are not the main problem; ECOWAS already aims at a common currency.

question: The absence of the rule of law in government will bring about ...
solution: The absence of the rule of law brings about human rights abuse. When rulers are not bound by the law, they can arrest, detain or punish people unfairly. Political apathy, corruption and treason may also occur, but the direct result of lawlessness in government is the abuse of people's rights.

question: The fundamental rights of citizens include the following EXCEPT.......

option.c: Free education, employment and freedom of thought

solution: The fundamental rights of citizens include life, liberty, property, association, speech and fair hearing. Free education, employment and freedom of thought are not listed as fundamental rights in the constitution — they are goals the state works towards. That is why that option is the exception.

question: The citizenship of a country could be acquired through_______
solution: Citizenship of a country can be acquired through birth and naturalisation. A person may be a citizen because he or she was born in the country or born to citizen parents, or may become a citizen later through naturalisation after meeting legal conditions. Registration and arbitration, presidential proclamation and parliamentary legislature are not the main ways.

question: A common feature of government is________
solution: A common feature of every government is the making of public policy. All governments, whether democratic or military, decide what to do about education, health, security and the economy. Separation of powers, an independent judiciary and a written constitution are not found in every system of government.

question: Under the 1999 constitution of Nigeria, the power to create local governments is vested in the .....
solution: Under the 1999 Constitution, the power to create local governments is vested in the State Assembly of each state. The State House of Assembly makes the law that creates local government areas and defines their functions. The National Assembly creates states, not local governments.

question: Who re-organised the Nigeria's four regions into twelve states in May 1967?
solution: General Yakubu Gowon re-organised Nigeria's four regions into twelve states in May 1967. The new states were created to bring government closer to the people and to weaken the pull of the regions. Ojukwu, Effiong and Balewa did not carry out this reorganisation.

question: The fees collected by local governments at motor parks represent ______
solution: The fees collected at motor parks by local governments are user charges. People who use the park pay a small fee for the service provided, such as parking and loading space. It is not income tax, a fine or a general levy imposed on all citizens.

question: Some pre-colonial Nigerian societies are described as stateless because ......

option.a: They had no formal governmental institutions
option.c: They had no definite political boundaries

solution: Some pre-colonial Nigerian societies are called stateless because they had no formal governmental institutions like a king, parliament or central authority. The Igbo and some middle-belt communities governed themselves through councils of elders, age-grades and family heads. They were independent and had boundaries, so those options are not the reason.

question: The first Nigerian constitution to provide for the Fundamental objectives and directive principles of the state policy was the _________
solution: The 1979 Constitution was the first Nigerian constitution to provide for the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy. It set out goals such as justice, equality and good welfare for citizens. The 1960 Constitution did not contain these principles, and the 1999 and 1989 constitutions came later.

question: The lbadan Conference of 1950 was convened to discuss the provisions of the ....
solution: The Ibadan Conference of 1950 was convened to discuss the provisions of the Macpherson Constitution. Representatives from different parts of Nigeria met to consider the draft constitution before it was approved. It was not about the Richards, Clifford or Lyttleton Constitution.

question: ____was the first Nigerian Permanent Representative to the United Nations.
solution: Chief Samuel Adebo was Nigeria's first Permanent Representative to the United Nations. He presented Nigeria's credentials at the UN soon after independence in 1960. Professor Ibrahim Gambari, Alhaji Yusuf Maitama Sule and General Joseph Garba served later.

question: Under the 1999 Constitution, the appointment of Ministers and Ambassadors must be ratified by the ........
solution: Under the 1999 Constitution, the appointment of Ministers and Ambassadors by the President must be ratified by the Senate. The Senate screens and confirms these nominees. The House of Representatives, the National Council of States and the Presidency do not ratify them.

question: The two military coups that toppled civilian regimes in Nigeria were those of ......
solution: The two military coups that toppled civilian regimes in Nigeria were those of January 1966 and December 1983. The first ended the First Republic, and the second ended the Second Republic. The 1975 and 1985 coups replaced military governments, not civilian ones.

question: Professor lbrahim Gambari was the Special Assistant to the United Nations Secretary General on____________
solution: Professor Ibrahim Gambari served as the UN Secretary-General's Special Assistant on African affairs. In that role he advised the UN on peace, development and conflict issues affecting Africa. He was not appointed specifically on security, political and social matters, or on the Economic Commission for Africa.

question: In the First Republic, the official opposition party was the ..........

option.a: National Council of Nigeria and Cameroons

solution: In the First Republic, the official opposition party was the Action Group (AG). It was led by Chief Obafemi Awolowo and criticised the ruling coalition. The NPC was the main ruling party, while the NCNC was part of the government coalition.
category: Political Parties and Party Politics in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: One argument against a multi-party system is the _______
solution: One argument against a multi-party system is the high cost of conducting elections. Many parties need money for campaigns, agents and logistics, and the country may hold expensive run-offs. It does not prevent foreign assistance or ban interest groups, and opposition is not by itself a bad thing in a democracy.

question: The independent National Electoral Commission has the power to prepare and maintain the register of.____
solution: The Independent National Electoral Commission has the power to prepare and maintain the register of voters. It registers eligible citizens, updates the voters' roll and issues voter cards. It does not register candidates, constituencies or political parties in the same way.

question: Before Nigeria became a republic, the highest body charged with the administration of justice was the......
solution: Before Nigeria became a republic, the highest body charged with the administration of justice was the Privy Council in London. Appeals from Nigerian courts could be taken to its Judicial Committee. After 1963, the Supreme Court of Nigeria became the highest court.
category: Institutions of Government in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: The highest grade in the Civil Service is known as the ............
solution: The highest grade in the Nigerian Civil Service is the administrative cadre. Administrative officers advise ministers, coordinate policy and head ministries and departments. The technical, executive and clerical cadres are lower grades with different duties.

question: After 1945, the demand of African nationalists changed from reform to independence because .....

option.a: The Second World War enhanced colonial rule
option.d: The Second World War boosted their morale

solution: After 1945, African nationalists changed their demand from reform to independence because the Second World War boosted their morale. Africans had fought for freedom abroad and saw that colonial powers could be defeated. The war also weakened Britain and France and spread ideas of freedom, so colonial rule did not become less oppressive.

question: Government by the wealthy is known as _________
solution: Government by the wealthy is known as plutocracy. In a plutocracy, rich people use their money to control political power. Democracy is rule by the people, oligarchy is rule by a small group, and aristocracy is rule by the noble or “best” class.

question: The main function of the Code of Conduct Bureau is to......

option.a: Give the police more powers to make arrests.
option.c: Give the judiciary more powers to discipline erring judges.
option.d: Protect public officers from the press

solution: The main function of the Code of Conduct Bureau is to ensure accountability in government business. It receives declarations of assets from public officers and checks that they do not abuse their office for private gain. It does not give the police or judiciary extra powers, and it does not protect officers from the press.

question: The Murtala/Obasanjo regime in Nigeria increased the number of states from....
solution: The Murtala/Obasanjo regime increased the number of states in Nigeria from 12 to 19 in 1976. The new states were created to bring government closer to the people and to correct imbalances. Nigeria later moved from 19 to 21 and then to 30 states, but that was under later governments.

question: In the legislative process, a bill is a ....
solution: In the legislative process, a bill is a proposal before the legislature. It becomes a law only after it has been debated, amended and signed by the President. A law already passed is an Act, while a motion is a proposal for discussion, not yet a bill.

question: Which of these is not a major characteristic of the rule of law?
solution: Separation of powers is not one of the classic characteristics of the rule of law. The rule of law means supremacy of the law, equality before the law and judicial independence, so that everyone is answerable to the same law. Separation of powers is a related democratic principle, but it is not listed as an element of the rule of law itself.

question: A policy formulated to guide relations with other nations is called
solution: A policy formulated to guide a country's relations with other nations is called a foreign policy. It covers how a country deals with other countries on trade, defence, diplomacy and international organisations. National, state and international policies are broader or different ideas.

question: The ________ as a new policy direction introduced by the French government that was aimed at granting more autonomy to its colonies under pressure from independence movements.
solution: The Loi Cadre was the new French policy that gave the colonies more internal autonomy in 1956, under pressure from independence movements. It allowed elected assemblies in the territories. The policy of assimilation tried to turn Africans into French citizens, while association was a later, looser policy.

question: The operations of a pressure group can be hindered by
solution: The operations of a pressure group can be hindered by poor leadership. If leaders are weak, divided or selfish, the group cannot organise members, raise funds or present its demands clearly. General observation, membership drive and spiritual forces are not the main obstacles.

question: The highest authority in the Yoruba pre-colonial era was the _____
solution: The highest authority in the Yoruba pre-colonial political system was the Oba. He ruled with the advice of the Oyomesi (council of chiefs) and the Ogboni cult, but he was the central political figure. The Balogun was a military commander, not the highest authority.

question: The basic unit of every political organization in the Igbo pre-colonial era was the
solution: The basic unit of political organisation in the Igbo pre-colonial system was the family. Families made up the compound, compounds made up the village, and villages formed larger groups. The ala was the earth goddess, the age-grade was an association, and the village council governed the village.

question: A political system built around land ownership is called
solution: A political system built around land ownership is called feudalism. Land was the main source of wealth and power, and those who owned it controlled those who worked on it. Monarchy is rule by a king, fascism is a forceful one-party system, and communalism is shared ownership by the community.

question: The absence of an independent judiciary is a feature of
solution: The absence of an independent judiciary is a feature of an oligarchy. When a small group holds power, it often controls the courts and uses them to protect its own interests. A limited monarchy, a capitalist system and a republican system can all allow an independent judiciary.

question: One of the features of rule of law is that an

option.b: accused is a culprit before trial

solution: One feature of the rule of law is that an accused person must receive fair hearing. Everyone is presumed innocent until proven guilty and must be allowed to defend himself in court. An accused is not automatically a culprit or offender before trial.

question: Nigeria's bicameral legislature featuring the House of Senate and House of Representatives is similar to ?
solution: Nigeria's bicameral legislature, with a Senate and a House of Representatives, is modelled on that of the USA. The United States Congress also has a Senate and a House of Representatives, and Nigeria copied the American presidential model. The UK also has two chambers, but it operates a parliamentary system.

question: A recurring principal objective of Nigerian foreign policy is
solution: A recurring principal objective of Nigerian foreign policy is promoting world peace with justice. Nigeria has taken part in peacekeeping and mediation in Africa and beyond. Defending friends, cementing relations and justifying supremacy are not stated objectives of the policy.

question: The Judicial Service Commission is vested with the power to recommend suitable persons for appointment of the _____
solution: The Judicial Service Commission recommends suitable persons for appointment to the National Judicial Council. The NJC then advises the President or Governor on the appointment of judges. It does not recommend directly to the Senate President or the Chief Justice.

question: The first Legislative Council in Nigeria was established by
solution: The first Legislative Council in Nigeria was established by the Clifford Constitution of 1922. It introduced the elective principle and allowed four elected Africans into the council. The Richards, Macpherson and Lyttleton constitutions came later and expanded the council.

question: The oversight function is performed by the
solution: The oversight function is performed by the legislature. It checks the executive by asking questions, investigating and approving budgets. The judiciary interprets laws, while the executive implements them.

question: Which one of these served as secretary general of the League of nations?
solution: Joseph Avenol served as Secretary-General of the League of Nations. He was a French diplomat who held the post in the 1930s and early 1940s. Trygve Lie, Javier Pérez de Cuéllar and Kurt Waldheim were Secretaries-General of the United Nations, not the League.

question: The ultimate goal of the nationalists was to
solution: The ultimate goal of the nationalists was to secure political independence for Nigeria. They wanted Nigerians to govern themselves instead of being ruled by Britain. Promoting education and African unity were important, but they were means to the main goal of independence.

question: The ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID) has its headquarters in
solution: The ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID) has its headquarters in Lomé, Togo. It was set up to provide loans and investment support for projects in West Africa. Abuja, Abidjan and Dakar host other institutions.

question: The aim of the International Labour Organization includes

option.d: coordinating the activities of organized agencies

solution: One aim of the International Labour Organization is advancing social and economic justice. The ILO works to improve working conditions, protect workers' rights and promote fair treatment in employment. Emergency assistance and coordinating all organised agencies belong to other bodies.

question: A one-party system helps to prevent
solution: A one-party system helps to prevent economic waste. With only one party, the country does not spend huge sums on competition between many parties. It may produce quick decisions and strong leadership, but it restricts political choice.

question: Nigeria is a major financier of which of the following?
solution: Nigeria is a major financier of the African Development Bank (AFDB). Nigeria is one of the bank's largest shareholders and supports its loans for African development. The IBRD, UNO and OPEC are not financed mainly by Nigeria.

question: Before the emergence of OAU as a regional body, Nigeria belonged to
solution: Before the OAU was formed, Nigeria belonged to the Monrovia group. This group favoured gradual cooperation and opposed immediate political union of African states. The Casablanca group wanted faster political integration.

question: The political rights of a citizen include the
solution: The political rights of a citizen include the right to vote. This allows citizens to choose their leaders and take part in government. Freedom of speech is a civil right, while the right to employment and the right to life are social and fundamental rights.

question: The French colonial policy aimed at changing Africans into French men was the policy of
solution: The French colonial policy aimed at changing Africans into French men was the policy of assimilation. France tried to replace African culture and institutions with French ones and to make a few Africans French citizens. Association was a later policy that respected local customs more.

question: Unitary system of government is best applicable to a/an
solution: A unitary system of government is best applicable to a homogeneous state. When the people share a common language, culture and history, one central government can rule without much conflict. A heterogeneous state usually needs a federal arrangement to accommodate its different groups.

question: An electoral system in which the winner must secure more than 50% of the vote is described as a/an
solution: An electoral system in which the winner must secure more than 50% of the vote is an absolute majority system. If no candidate reaches 50%, a run-off is held between the leading candidates. A plurality system only requires the highest number of votes, not a majority.

question: A system of government in which a single person or a group who governs has unlimited power is a
solution: A system of government in which a single person or a small group has unlimited power is an autocracy. The ruler is not accountable to the people or to the law. Oligarchy is rule by a few, aristocracy by nobles, and a republic has elected leaders.

question: One of these is a major problem of the Nigerian civil service
solution: One major problem of the Nigerian civil service is corruption. Some officials demand bribes, inflate contracts or misuse public funds, which weakens service delivery. Inadequate personnel and weak leadership can occur, but corruption is the most widely recognised problem.

question: The 1976 Local Government Reforms made the Nigerian local government become
solution: The 1976 Local Government Reforms made local governments recipients of statutory allocations from the Federation Account. This gave them a guaranteed share of national revenue. They did not become fully autonomous or a fourth tier, and the number 774 came later.

question: The philosophy behind Nigerian federalism is
solution: The philosophy behind Nigerian federalism is unity in diversity. Federalism allows different ethnic and regional groups to keep their identities while sharing one country and one central government. It was not designed for sectional development or colonial rule.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: On 1 October 1995, Abacha announced a three-year program for return to civilian rule. Parties were allowed to form in July 1998. Which of the following parties was not registered by the Provisional Ruling Council?
solution: Action Congress was not registered by the Provisional Ruling Council in 1998. The parties registered then included the Alliance for Democracy, the All People's Party and the People's Democratic Party. Action Congress was formed later, in 2006.
category: Political Parties and Party Politics in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: The conference convened to discuss the provisions of the Macpherson Constitution was held in?
solution: The conference convened to discuss the provisions of the Macpherson Constitution was held in Ibadan in 1950. It brought together representatives from the regions to review the draft. London, Calabar and Lagos hosted other conferences or events.

question: In a federal system of government, legislative items constitutionally reserved for only the central government fall under the _________ list.
solution: In a federal system, legislative items reserved for only the central government fall under the exclusive list. Only the federal government can legislate on them, for example defence and currency. The concurrent list is shared, while the residual list belongs to the states.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: The defence pact between Nigeria and Britain was cancelled in the year
solution: The defence pact between Nigeria and Britain was cancelled in 1962. Nigerians opposed the pact because it allowed Britain to keep military influence over the country. It was signed at independence in 1960 but cancelled two years later.

question: A major consequence of the privatization exercise in Nigeria is

option.a: the collapse of the Nigerian economy

solution: A major consequence of the privatisation exercise in Nigeria is mass retrenchment of labour. When government companies were sold to private owners, many workers lost their jobs as the new owners cut costs. Privatisation did not collapse the economy in the way suggested.

question: One of the constitutional requirements for the registration of political parties in Nigeria is ______

option.a: provision for review of party manifesto
option.d: national presence in the federal capital territory

solution: One constitutional requirement for registering a political party in Nigeria is national presence in the Federal Capital Territory. A party must have offices and members in many parts of the country, including Abuja, to show that it is truly national. Having offices in only twelve states or a manifesto review is not the requirement.

question: The highest body which performed legislative functions under Babangida Regime was
solution: The highest body that performed legislative functions under the Babangida regime was the Armed Forces Ruling Council (AFRC). It made decrees and controlled the government. The National Council of State and the Council of Ministers were advisory or executive bodies, not the law-making body.

question: A group of people with different natures, opinions, and goals with complicated networks of social relation
solution: A group of people with different natures, opinions and goals, linked by a complicated network of social relations, is a society. Society is the broad community within which other groups exist. A union or association is a smaller organised group, and a state is a political organisation with sovereignty.

question: The process of pressure groups trying to influence legislation is known as
solution: The process of pressure groups trying to influence legislation is known as lobbying. They meet legislators, send letters and run campaigns to persuade them to support their cause. An ultimatum, dialogue and strike are other methods, but lobbying is the direct attempt to influence law-making.

question: A constitution that requires specific statutory procedures for amendment is said to be
solution: A constitution that requires special statutory procedures for amendment is said to be rigid. It cannot be changed by an ordinary law; a special majority or referendum is needed. A flexible constitution can be amended easily, while written and unwritten describe the form, not the amendment procedure.

question: The Security Council of the United Nations Organization has
solution: The Security Council of the United Nations has five permanent members. They are the United States, Britain, France, Russia and China, and each has veto power. The other members are elected for two-year terms, making fifteen members in all.

question: When an election fails to produce a clear winner, the process of determining a winner is called
solution: When an election does not produce a clear winner, a re-run election is held to decide the winner. A bye-election fills a seat that becomes vacant after the main election, while a recall is a process for removing an elected officer. A referendum is a public vote on an issue, not a way of choosing between candidates.

question: The Ijaw people of pre-colonial Nigeria were organized into?
solution: The Ijaw people of pre-colonial Nigeria were organised into clans. Each clan was made up of related families and was led by elders and chiefs. They did not build large federations or centralised chiefdoms like some other groups.

question: The zoning system in Nigerian politics refers to

option.a: the rotation of power among different regions
option.b: the process of selecting party leaders

solution: The zoning system in Nigerian politics refers to the rotation of power among different regions. Political offices are shared among the geopolitical zones so that no single area dominates. It is not about selecting party leaders, campaign funds or proportional representation.

question: The electoral commission that organized the 1979 general elections was
solution: The electoral commission that organised the 1979 general elections was FEDECO, the Federal Electoral Commission. INEC was created later, in 1998, and NECON was used in the aborted Third Republic. ECN was an economic body, not an electoral commission.

question: Which of the following is a limitation of pressure groups?

option.a: They only represent the interests of the wealthy.
option.b: They have no influence on the government policies
option.c: They may prioritize their own interests over the public interest
option.d: They often resort to violent tactics

solution: One limitation of pressure groups is that they may put their own interests above the public interest. A group may push for policies that benefit its members even when those policies harm the wider society. They do have influence, and most do not use violence, so those options are not correct.

question: Which of the following is a characteristic of pressure groups?

option.a: They aim to gain political power
option.b: They are funded by the government
option.d: They represent the interest of a specific section of the society

solution: A characteristic of pressure groups is that they represent the interest of a specific section of society. For example, a teachers' union speaks for teachers. They do not aim to capture political power, they are not funded by government, and they are not political parties.

question: The constitutional amendment process in Nigeria requires the approval of
solution: The constitutional amendment process in Nigeria requires the approval of the National Assembly. A bill to amend the constitution must be supported by a special majority in both chambers and by the state assemblies. INEC, the President and the Supreme Court do not amend the constitution.

question: In which system of government is the executive and legislature fused?
solution: The executive and legislature are fused in the cabinet (parliamentary) system. Ministers are members of parliament and form the executive, so the same people sit in both arms. In a presidential system the two arms are separate.

question: Which Nigerian leader played a significant role in mediating peace talks during the Liberian civil war?
solution: Ibrahim Babangida played a significant role in mediating peace talks during the Liberian civil war. Nigeria, under his military government, led the ECOMOG peacekeeping force that helped restore order in Liberia. Obasanjo, Buhari and Jonathan were not the leaders at that time.

question: The Commonwealth of Nations was initially known as
solution: The Commonwealth of Nations was initially known as the British Commonwealth. It began as a group of former British colonies that kept links with Britain. It was not called the Imperial Commonwealth, Commonwealth Realm or League of Nations.

question: Which political party was known for its socialist ideology and populist policies in the 1980s?
solution: The People's Redemption Party (PRP) was known for its socialist ideology and populist policies in the 1980s. Led by Mallam Aminu Kano, it appealed to ordinary people and criticised elitist rule. The other parties were more conservative.
category: Political Parties and Party Politics in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: Which of the following is an example of a public pressure group?
solution: Amnesty International is an example of a public pressure group because it campaigns for the human rights of everybody. It does not seek power for itself and is not tied to any political party. The other options are organisations with narrower or different aims.

question: In a communist system, who owns and controls the means of production?
solution: In a communist system, the government owns and controls the means of production. Factories, land and businesses belong to the state on behalf of the people. Private individuals and corporations do not control the economy in communism.

question: Which of the following is a concurrent power in the Nigerian federal system?
solution: Education and healthcare are concurrent powers in Nigeria's federal system. This means both the federal and state governments can make laws about them. Currency, foreign affairs and defence are exclusive federal powers.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: The term 'lobbying' refers to
solution: Lobbying means seeking to influence government decisions, especially the making of laws. Pressure groups meet legislators, send letters and run campaigns to persuade them. It is not the same as campaigning for office or organising a protest movement.

question: Jus Sanguinis is a principle that grants citizenship based on
solution: Jus sanguinis grants citizenship based on parental citizenship — a child becomes a citizen because his or her parents are citizens. Citizenship based on place of birth is jus soli. Ethnic background and length of residency are not what the term means.

question: Which constitution established the Public Service Commission?
solution: The 1963 Constitution established the Public Service Commission. It set up commissions to handle the appointment, promotion and discipline of civil servants. The 1979, 1999 and 1989 constitutions came later and continued the commissions.

question: Which of the following is a function of the Public Complaints Commission?
solution: One function of the Public Complaints Commission is conducting investigations and enquiries into complaints about administrative injustice. It acts as the ombudsman and recommends remedies. It does not manage transport, enforce criminal laws or implement foreign policy.

question: Which of the following was a significant trade commodity in the pre-colonial Kingdom of Benin?
solution: Ivory was a significant trade commodity in the pre-colonial Kingdom of Benin. Benin craftsmen used ivory for carvings, and it was traded with Europeans. Gold, rubber and salt were important in other places or later periods.

question: which pre-colonial Nigerian Kingdom was known for its artistic and cultural achievement?
solution: The pre-colonial kingdom known for its artistic and cultural achievement was Benin. Benin is famous for its bronze plaques, ivory carvings and royal art. Nupe, Igbo and Kanem-Bornu had their own cultures, but Benin is best known for this.

question: Judges in the International Court of Justice are appointed for a period of _____ years.
solution: Judges of the International Court of Justice are appointed for nine years. They may be re-elected after their term. The court sits at The Hague and settles disputes between states.

question: Which institution is responsible for the regulation and supervision of capital markets in Nigeria?
solution: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) regulates and supervises the capital market in Nigeria. It licenses operators, protects investors and ensures fair dealing. The Nigerian Stock Exchange is a market, while the FRCN and CAC handle other matters.
category: Institutions of Government in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: Without presidential assent, the legislature can pass a bill into law with the votes of ______ majority
solution: Without presidential assent, the legislature can pass a bill into law with a two-thirds majority of each chamber. This is how the legislature can override a presidential veto. One-fifth, one-third and an absolute majority are not enough.

question: The process of forming public opinion is known as
solution: The process of forming public opinion is known as socialisation. Family, school, religion, the media and peer groups shape the views people hold about politics. Polling measures opinion, while mobilisation and persuasion are ways of influencing it.

question: Nigeria's foreign policy is guided by the principle of
solution: Nigeria's foreign policy is guided by the principle of national interest. The country protects its security, economy and citizens in whatever it does abroad. Military dominance, economic self-sufficiency and territorial expansion are not the guiding principle.

question: During the cold war, Nigeria's foreign policy was characterized by
solution: During the Cold War, Nigeria's foreign policy was characterised by neutrality and non-alignment. Nigeria refused to join either the Western or the Soviet bloc. It did not align with the United States or the Soviet Union, and it did not pursue colonial interests.

question: Which committee is responsible for the detailed scrutiny of a bill?
solution: The standing committee is responsible for the detailed scrutiny of a bill. After the second reading, a bill is sent to the appropriate standing committee, which examines it clause by clause. Ad hoc, joint and select committees may be used for special purposes, but standing committees do the routine detailed work.

question: The 1963 constitution created a list of powers exclusively reserved for the
solution: The 1963 Constitution created a list of powers exclusively reserved for the federal government. These included defence, foreign affairs and currency. State and regional governments handled other matters, while local governments had no exclusive list.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: Which of the following statements about pressure groups is true?

option.a: They have no influence on the decision-making process
option.b: They can have both positive and negative impact on the government
option.c: They operate independently of the government
option.d: They are only concerned with social issues

solution: A true statement about pressure groups is that they can have both positive and negative effects on government. They may help government understand people's needs, but they can also push selfish demands. They do have influence, and they are not only concerned with social issues.

question: Which of the following is not a source of public opinion?
solution: Opinion polls are not a source of public opinion; they are a way of measuring it. Sources that help form opinion include academic journals, social media and political parties. Polls simply find out what people already think.

question: The National assembly is composed of how many chambers?
solution: The National Assembly is composed of two chambers: the Senate and the House of Representatives. This makes it a bicameral legislature. It does not have one, three or four chambers.

question: The process of decolonization in Nigeria was hugely impacted by
solution: The process of decolonisation in Nigeria was hugely impacted by World War II. The war weakened the colonial powers, exposed their weaknesses and spread ideas of freedom and self-rule. The Renaissance, World War I and the Cold War had less direct impact.

question: The civil service in Nigeria operates under the principle of
solution: The civil service in Nigeria operates under the principle of meritocracy. Jobs are supposed to be given on the basis of qualifications and performance through the Civil Service Commission. Autonomy and separation of powers are different ideas.

question: Which of the following countries operate a direct democracy?
solution: Switzerland is known for operating a direct democracy. Citizens vote directly on many important issues through referendums. Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States mainly use representative democracy.

question: Which of the following is the basic unit of a local government in Nigeria?
solution: The basic unit of a local government in Nigeria is the ward. A local government area is divided into wards, and each ward is represented by a councillor. State assemblies, LCDAs and the Ministry of Local Government are not the basic unit.

question: Which of the following is a fundamental principle of democratic governance?
solution: Citizen participation is a fundamental principle of democratic governance. Democracy works best when people take part in elections, debates and community decisions. Centralised decision-making, censorship and authoritarianism are opposite to democracy.

question: The judiciary checks the other arms of government through
solution: The judiciary checks the other arms of government through judicial review. Courts can examine laws and actions of the executive and declare them unconstitutional. Judicial recall and judicial precedence are not the correct terms for this power.

question: Which African country successfully resisted European imperialism and maintained its independence?
solution: Ethiopia successfully resisted European imperialism and maintained its independence. It defeated Italy at the Battle of Adwa in 1896 and remained free. Ghana, Kenya and Algeria were all colonised.

question: What is the primary source of revenue for the local government in Nigeria?
solution: The primary source of revenue for local governments in Nigeria is federal government allocations. Local governments receive a statutory share of the Federation Account. Taxes, foreign grants and oil revenue are smaller or indirect sources.

question: Public corporations and parastatals are typically established by
solution: Public corporations and parastatals are typically established by legislative acts and statutes. The law spells out their powers, functions and how they are funded. Private individuals, trade unions and international organisations do not establish them.

question: The main argument against the 1999 Constitution is that

option.a: it was imposed by the military
option.d: It did not create additional states

solution: The main argument against the 1999 Constitution is that it was imposed by the military. It was promulgated by the military government of General Abdulsalami Abubakar in 1999 rather than being debated and agreed by elected representatives of the people. The immunity clause and the cost of running the constitution are complaints too, but they are not the main argument.

question: An economic system that encourages state ownership and control of the means of production is
solution: An economic system that encourages state ownership and control of the means of production is socialism. In socialism the government owns or strongly controls factories, land and key businesses so that wealth can be shared more equally. Capitalism favours private ownership, communism goes further with total state control, and fascism is a political system rather than an economic one.

question: Nigeria played fundamental roles in the creation of
solution: Nigeria played a fundamental role in the creation of ECOWAS, the Economic Community of West African States. Nigeria and Togo led the move, and the treaty was signed in Lagos in 1975. Nigeria did not create OPEC, the UN or the Commonwealth; those bodies already existed before Nigeria joined them.

question: A major instrument designed to promote the workings of Nigerian federalism is
solution: A major instrument designed to promote the workings of Nigerian federalism is the Federal Character Commission. It ensures that appointments and national institutions reflect the different states and ethnic groups of the country, so that no section feels excluded. The National Judicial Council, National Assembly Commission and National Defence Council serve other purposes.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: A union of states with a common recognised authority is
solution: A union of states with a common recognised authority is a federal system. In a federation, the central government and the component states each have their own powers, and both are recognised by the constitution. A unitary system has one central government, while a confederation gives the centre very little power over the states.

question: The Aburi Accord was a popular phrase during the administration of
solution: The Aburi Accord was a popular phrase during the administration of Yakubu Gowon. It was the agreement reached at Aburi, Ghana, in 1967 between the federal military government and the Eastern Region to try to settle their differences. Ironsi, Murtala Muhammed and Obasanjo were not in power when the accord was made.

question: The fundamental objective guiding a nation's foreign policy is
solution: The fundamental objective guiding a nation's foreign policy is national interest. Every country acts abroad to protect its security, economy and citizens. Foreign, African and colonial interests may influence policy, but they are not the guiding objective.

question: An agent in which the state undertakes direct political socialisation is the
solution: An agent through which the state undertakes direct political socialisation is the school. Schools teach civic education, national history and rules of behaviour, and they gather children of different backgrounds together. The church, peer groups and the mass media also shape political attitudes, but the school is the agent the state uses directly.

question: The collective views of the citizens on a specific national matter is
solution: The collective views of the citizens on a specific national matter is public opinion. It is what most people in the country think about an issue such as a new law or a government policy. Group opinions belong to smaller groups, while collective responsibility is about shared blame or praise.

question: Which local government reform in Nigeria prevented traditional rulers from engaging in politics?
solution: The 1976 Local Government Reform prevented traditional rulers from engaging in partisan politics. It separated the traditional council from the local government council so that chiefs would advise on tradition and custom rather than run party politics. The 1960, 1963 and 1979 reforms did not make this change.

question: The power of prerogative of mercy rests with the
solution: The power of prerogative of mercy rests with the executive. The President at the federal level, or a Governor at the state level, can pardon or reduce the punishment of a convicted person. The legislature makes laws, the judiciary interprets them, and the National Assembly is part of the legislature.

question: Absence of a Red-tape is a merit of
solution: Absence of red tape is a merit of a unitary structure. A unitary system has one central government and fewer layers of authority, so decisions are taken quickly and there is less bureaucratic delay. Federal and confederal systems share power among several governments, which can slow down decisions.

question: The most effective instrument adopted by Nigeria against the East-West Cold War in the 1960s was
solution: The most effective instrument adopted by Nigeria against the East-West Cold War in the 1960s was the non-alignment policy. Nigeria refused to join either the Western or the Soviet bloc and instead tried to stay neutral while protecting African interests. Good neighbourliness and the anti-apartheid stance were parts of policy, but non-alignment was the direct answer to the Cold War.

question: Lawyers recruited into the civil service belong to the
solution: Lawyers recruited into the civil service belong to the professional class. This class includes doctors, lawyers, engineers and other specialists who use their professional training in government service. The administrative class coordinates policy, while the executive and clerical classes handle routine duties.

question: The Nigerian Youth Movement pursued its objectives through the use of
solution: The Nigerian Youth Movement pursued its objectives mainly through the use of newspapers. It used its newspaper, the Daily Service, to educate Nigerians and criticise colonial rule. Protest, radio and strike actions were used by other groups or at other times.

question: A naturalised citizen can lose his citizenship if found guilty of
solution: A naturalised citizen can lose his citizenship if found guilty of treason. Treason is a serious crime against the state, such as trying to overthrow the government by force or waging war against the country. Evading tax, electoral violence and loitering are offences, but they do not automatically remove citizenship.

question: Shehu Shagari won the 1979 Presidential Election under
solution: Shehu Shagari won the 1979 Presidential Election under the NPN, the National Party of Nigeria. The NPN was the largest party in the Second Republic and formed the federal government. UPN, NPP and GNPP were rival parties led by other politicians.
category: Political Parties and Party Politics in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: Nigerian Ports Authority is an example of
solution: The Nigerian Ports Authority is an example of a public corporation. It is a government-owned body set up by law to provide an essential service, in this case managing the country's ports. It is not part of the civil service or the public service, and there is no separate maritime corporation.

question: One of the internal factors that led to the rise and growth of nationalism in Nigeria was
solution: One internal factor that led to the rise and growth of nationalism in Nigeria was the return of ex-service men. Nigerians who fought for Britain in the World Wars came home with new ideas about freedom and equality, and some joined the nationalist struggle. The British Labour Party, the Pan-African Congress and India's independence were external factors.

question: The bipolar world was a major factor for the formation of
solution: The bipolar world was a major factor for the formation of the Non-Aligned Movement. When the world split into a Western bloc led by the USA and an Eastern bloc led by the Soviet Union, many new nations chose to stay outside both camps. The Technical Aid Corps, NEPAD and ECOMOG were created for other purposes.

question: Under the Hausa pre-colonial administration, the office of the Prime Minister is usually occupied by
solution: In the Hausa pre-colonial administration, the office of the Prime Minister was usually occupied by the Waziri. The Waziri was the chief adviser and the most senior official after the Emir, and he helped to run the government. The Sarki was the king, the Galadima was in charge of the capital, and the Madawaki was the commander of the cavalry.

question: Which of these colonial constitutions in Nigeria endured for the longest period?
solution: The colonial constitution that endured for the longest period was the Clifford Constitution of 1922. It remained in force for about twenty-four years, until it was replaced by the Richards Constitution in 1946. The Richards, Macpherson and Lyttleton constitutions each lasted only a few years.

question: The leader of the Oyo Mesi in the Yoruba pre-colonial political system was
solution: The leader of the Oyo Mesi in the Yoruba pre-colonial political system was the Bashorun. The Oyo Mesi was the council of seven senior chiefs that advised the Alaafin and could even ask him to abdicate. The Aremo was the crown prince, the Oba was the ruler, and the Baale headed a town or village.

question: ECOWAS secretariat is located in
solution: The ECOWAS secretariat is located in Abuja, Nigeria. The headquarters moved to Abuja when Nigeria's capital changed from Lagos, and the secretariat later became the ECOWAS Commission. Accra, Niamey and Cotonou host other institutions or meetings.

question: The fragmented nature of the Igbo pre-colonial political system qualified it to be described as
solution: The fragmented nature of the Igbo pre-colonial political system qualified it to be described as acephalous. This means it had no single all-powerful head or king. Authority was shared among family heads, village councils, age grades and title societies. It was not centralised, ceremonial or a republic in the modern sense.

question: The judgement that ceded and transferred Bakassi legal title from Nigeria to Cameroon was delivered by

option.b: Court of Justice of the African Union

solution: The judgment that ceded Bakassi and transferred legal title from Nigeria to Cameroon was delivered by the International Court of Justice (ICJ). The court sat at The Hague and ruled in 2002, and the peninsula was handed over in 2008. The ECOWAS Court, the African Union Court and the ICC deal with different matters.

question: Dual citizenship was a feature of the
solution: Dual citizenship was a feature of the French colonial system. Under the policy of assimilation, some Africans were granted French citizenship while still belonging to their own territories, so they held two citizenships. The British system generally did not grant this double status.

question: Strike action is mostly used by
solution: Strike action is mostly used by pressure groups, especially trade unions. Workers stop work to force the government or an employer to meet their demands, such as better pay or working conditions. Political parties, traders and parliamentarians use other methods to press their case.

question: The political subjugation and economic exploitation of a people is known as
solution: The political subjugation and economic exploitation of a people is known as colonialism. One country takes over another, rules its people and uses its resources for the benefit of the colonial power. Neo-colonialism is indirect control after independence, apartheid was racial separation in South Africa, and indirect rule was a method of colonial administration.

question: A major problem affecting Local government in Nigeria today is
solution: A major problem affecting local government in Nigeria today is state government interference. State governors often control local government funds, dissolve councils and influence their decisions, which weakens local autonomy. Resource control, personnel management and revenue allocation are related issues, but interference from the state is the major problem.

question: NEPAD stands for

option.a: New Economic Programmes for African Development
option.c: New Economic Partnerships for African Development

solution: NEPAD stands for New Partnership for Africa's Development. It is an African programme launched in 2001 to promote good governance, investment and economic growth on the continent. The other options alter the words and are not the correct name.

question: Lack of separation of power is a feature of
solution: Lack of separation of power is a feature of a military government. Military rulers combine executive, legislative and sometimes judicial powers in one command structure, and they rule by decrees rather than by separate arms of government. Presidential, cabinet and democratic systems all separate or share powers in different ways.

question: Public corporations in Nigeria are established through
solution: Public corporations in Nigeria are established through an Act of Parliament. The law creates the corporation, states its functions, powers and how it will be funded. An executive order, an Order-in-Council or a judicial review cannot create a public corporation.

question: The rationale behind the adoption of a federal system of government in Nigeria is to
solution: The rationale behind the adoption of a federal system in Nigeria is to promote unity in diversity. Federalism allows many ethnic groups and regions to keep their identities while sharing one country and one central government. Promoting state autonomy and creating more states are effects, not the main reason.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: Which of these is a major challenge of public corporations in Nigeria?
solution: A major challenge of public corporations in Nigeria is political interference. Politicians and governments often meddle in the running of corporations, appoint their supporters and influence contracts, which reduces efficiency. Political instability, staff shortages and industrial disputes also occur, but interference is the major challenge.

question: The electoral process in a representative government does NOT include
solution: The electoral process in a representative government does not include registration of birth. Elections require free and fair voting, a free press and an independent electoral commission. Birth registration is a civil record and has nothing to do with conducting an election.

question: Price stability in the international oil market is the major objective of the
solution: Price stability in the international oil market is the major objective of OPEC, the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries. OPEC coordinates the petroleum policies of its members and tries to keep oil prices steady so that both producers and consumers are protected. The UN, WTO and AU deal with wider political, trade and continental matters.

question: The organs of ECOWAS do NOT include the
solution: The organs of ECOWAS do not include a body called the Conference. Its main organs include the Authority of Heads of State and Government, the Council of Ministers, the Community Tribunal, the Executive Secretariat (now Commission) and the Community Parliament. A conference is a meeting, not an organ of the community.

question: Delegated legislation can be regulated through
solution: Delegated legislation can be regulated through legislative control. The parliament that delegates power keeps an eye on it by approving the parent Act, setting limits in the Act and using committees to review the rules made.
