Ministerial, executive and judicial controls also exist, but the legislature is the body that grants and supervises the delegated power.

question: The first constitution to introduce a presidential system was the
solution: The first constitution to introduce a presidential system in Nigeria was the 1979 Constitution. It created an executive President who was both head of state and head of government, with a clear separation from the legislature. The 1963 Constitution kept the parliamentary system, and the 1999 Constitution continued the presidential model.

question: Political power in a democracy is derived from the
solution: Political power in a democracy is derived from the people. Citizens choose their leaders through elections, and the government rules with the consent of the governed. Traditional rulers, institutions and the barrel of the gun are not the source of power in a democracy.

question: The application of the rule of law can be hindered by
solution: The application of the rule of law can be hindered by diplomatic immunity. Foreign diplomats cannot be arrested or tried in the host country's ordinary courts, so the law cannot be applied to them in the same way as to citizens. Age, religion and a free press do not stop the rule of law from working.

question: The group that had the best egalitarian traditional political system is the
solution: The group with the best egalitarian traditional political system was the Igbo. Igbo communities had no single all-powerful king; decisions were taken by family heads, village assemblies, age grades and title societies, so people had a say in government. The Yoruba, Edo and Hausa systems were more centralised around kings and emirs.

question: Colonial policy of assimilation was introduced in Africa by the
solution: The colonial policy of assimilation was introduced in Africa by the French. France tried to turn a small group of Africans into French citizens by teaching them French language, culture and law. The Portuguese, British and Germans used different colonial policies.

question: OPEC was formed by some oil producing nations in
solution: OPEC was formed by some oil-producing nations in 1960. The Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries was created at the Baghdad Conference in September 1960 by five countries, including Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait and Venezuela. Nigeria joined later, in 1971.

question: One of the major reasons for colonialism in Africa was
solution: One of the major reasons for colonialism in Africa was economic interest. European powers wanted raw materials, markets for their goods, land and cheap labour. Religious and humanitarian reasons were sometimes given, but the driving motive was economic gain.

question: The Independent National Electoral Commission is responsible for
solution: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is responsible for conducting general elections. It registers voters and parties, organises polls and announces results. Swearing in elected members is done by judges, population census is handled by the NPC, and impeachment is a legislative process.

question: Census controversy was one of the factors that contributed to the military intervention in
solution: Census controversy was one of the factors that contributed to military intervention in 1966. The disputed 1962/63 census deepened regional mistrust and helped create the crisis that led to the January 1966 coup. The other dates refer to later events.

question: An important characteristic of state is
solution: An important characteristic of a state is sovereignty. A state has supreme power over its own affairs and is not subject to another state. A strong military, a treasury and a shared culture may exist in a state, but they are not the defining characteristic.

question: The highest court in the Hausa-Fulani political system was presided by
solution: In the Hausa-Fulani political system, the highest court was presided over by the Emir. The Emir was the supreme political and judicial authority in the emirate, and important cases were brought before him. The Hakimi was a district head, while the Ulamma were religious scholars.

question: The War Against Indiscipline campaign was launched by the military regime of
solution: The War Against Indiscipline campaign was launched by the military regime of General Muhammadu Buhari. It began in 1984 and urged Nigerians to be orderly, punctual, patriotic and hardworking. Obasanjo, Abacha and Babangida led at other times.

question: A community that cooperates and harnesses its resources together is said to be practising
solution: A community that cooperates and harnesses its resources together is practising communalism. In communalism, people own resources in common and work together for the good of the whole community. Capitalism is private ownership, socialism is state ownership, and communism is a more complete form of collective ownership.

question: Party coalition is common in a
solution: Party coalition is common in a multi-party system. When many parties compete and none wins a clear majority, two or more parties join together to form a government. Zero-party, two-party and one-party systems leave little or no room for coalitions.

question: Democracy is a system in which the
solution: Democracy is a system in which there is majority rule. Decisions are taken by the greater number of people, usually through elected representatives, while the rights of the minority are still protected. Minority rule is the opposite of democracy.

question: Local Government Areas in Nigeria are by act of the 1999 constitution a/ an
solution: By the 1999 Constitution, Local Government Areas in Nigeria are an autonomous level of government. The constitution recognises them as the third tier of government with their own powers and responsibilities. They are not mere appendages of the central or state government.

question: Nigeria applies soft diplomacy in Africa through
solution: Nigeria applies soft diplomacy in Africa through the Technical Aid Corps programme. Under this scheme Nigeria sends doctors, teachers, engineers and other professionals to assist other African countries, winning goodwill without using force. Encouraging capitalism, bilateral relations and disengagement from peacekeeping are not the same thing.

question: The use of Prime Minister as the head of Government is associated with which system of governance?
solution: The use of a Prime Minister as head of government is associated with the parliamentary system. In this system the Prime Minister is the leader of the majority party in parliament and governs with a cabinet drawn from parliament. A presidential system has an executive President instead, and a monarchy is rule by a king or queen.

question: A permanent civil service
solution: A permanent civil service makes continuity of government possible. Civil servants stay in office when governments change, so policies and records are not lost and the new government can continue the work of the old one. It does not exist to make officials arrogant or to promote ethnic domination.

question: Which of the following is NOT a duty of citizens in a state?
solution: Spying on the state is not a duty of a citizen. Citizens are expected to prevent crime, vote in elections and pay their taxes. Spying on one's own country is a crime, not a civic duty.

question: A permanent structure that facilitates continuity in governance is the
solution: The permanent structure that facilitates continuity in governance is the civil service. Its officials are recruited on merit and remain in office across changes of government, keeping records and carrying on public administration. The military, public corporations and the judiciary do not serve this purpose in the same way.

question: Written constitutions are always
solution: Written constitutions are always rigid in the sense that they are amended by a special procedure. Because a written constitution is a single formal document, changing it requires a special majority, a referendum or the approval of state assemblies, not just an ordinary law. Flexible constitutions are usually unwritten and can be changed easily.

question: The right to vote and be voted in an election is
solution: The right to vote and be voted for in an election is called franchise. It is the legal right of qualified citizens to take part in elections. An election right, a constitutional right and inheritance are not the specific name for this right.

question: Sovereignty refers to the

option.a: the supreme power of a state to use force in order to enforce obedience
option.b: the supreme power of a state to negotiate with other states
option.c: the supreme power of a state to govern other nations
option.d: the supreme power and authority of a state over its own affairs

solution: Sovereignty refers to the supreme power and authority of a state over its own affairs. A sovereign state makes its own laws and decisions without taking orders from another state. Using force, negotiating with other states and governing other nations are parts of what a state may do, but they are not the definition of sovereignty.

question: Which of these is a professional pressure group in Nigeria?
solution: The Nigerian Union of Teachers (NUT) is a professional pressure group. It is made up of people in the teaching profession and works to protect their interests and improve education. The Nigeria Labour Congress is a trade union federation, the Manufacturers Association is a business group, and the Arewa Consultative Forum is a socio-cultural group.

question: Which of the following promotes private ownership of properties?
solution: Capitalism promotes private ownership of property. Individuals and companies own land, factories and businesses and are free to make profit. Communalism, socialism and feudalism all place ownership or control in the community, the state or a land-owning class.

question: When a pressure group is made up of people of the same profession, it is called
solution: When a pressure group is made up of people of the same profession, it is called an occupation group. Examples are the Nigerian Medical Association and the Nigerian Bar Association. Promotional groups campaign for causes, interest groups protect members' interests, and associational groups are formally organised bodies.

question: The head of the legislative arm at the third tier of government in Nigeria is the
solution: The head of the legislative arm at the third tier of government in Nigeria is the Leader. In a local government council, the Chairman heads the executive while the Leader heads the legislative council that makes bye-laws. The Speaker and President belong to other levels of government.

question: Laws made by the local government, public corporations and ministries is a
solution: Laws made by local governments, public corporations and ministries are called bye-laws. They are subsidiary laws made under powers given by an Act, and they apply to a particular area or body. Decrees are made by military governments, while public laws and enactments are made by the legislature.

question: The umbrella body for relations among all African countries is
solution: The umbrella body for relations among all African countries is the African Union (AU). It replaced the Organisation of African Unity in 2002 and has members from across the continent. The Commonwealth, ECOWAS and the UN are wider or smaller bodies.

question: The first past the post system of voting is also referred to as
solution: The first past the post system of voting is also referred to as the simple majority method. The candidate with the highest number of votes wins, even if he or she does not get more than half of all the votes cast. A single transferable vote, an alternative vote and a second ballot are different electoral systems.

question: Before the 1976 reforms, local government administration in Nigeria was characterised by
solution: Before the 1976 reforms, local government administration in Nigeria was characterised by high centralisation. The regional and state governments controlled local councils, appointed their officials and decided their finances. Democratic elections, standardised structures and autonomy in decision making came with the reforms.

question: An organised group of citizens acting together and seeking to obtain the control of government is a
solution: An organised group of citizens acting together and seeking to obtain control of government is a political party. A party contests elections, presents a manifesto and tries to form the government. Civil society, labour unions and student unions may campaign on issues, but they do not seek to control government.

question: Fascism and Nazism are ideologies that were promoted respectively by
solution: Fascism and Nazism were promoted respectively by Mussolini and Hitler. Mussolini led the fascist movement in Italy, and Hitler led the Nazi movement in Germany. Mein Kampf was Hitler's book, not a person, and the other names are not correct.

question: Which of the following factors can limit the application of the rule of law?
solution: Court congestion can limit the application of the rule of law. When courts are overloaded with cases, trials are delayed and people may wait years for justice, which weakens the idea that the law applies promptly to all. Strike action, foreign influence and a free press do not directly prevent the law from being applied.

question: One major feature of Nigerian foreign policy is

option.c: non-alignment with any of the power blocs

solution: One major feature of Nigerian foreign policy is non-alignment with any of the power blocs. Nigeria has tried to stay independent of the Western and Eastern blocs and to support African causes. Lack of cooperation, unrealistic economic policy and non-developing policies are not features of the policy.

question: The elective principle was first introduced under
solution: The elective principle was first introduced under the Clifford Constitution of 1922. It allowed a small number of Africans to be elected to the Legislative Council, the first time elections were used in Nigeria. The Richards, Macpherson and Lyttleton constitutions came later and widened the principle.

question: Adjudication is the primary responsibility of the
solution: Adjudication is the primary responsibility of the judiciary. Judges hear cases, interpret the law and decide disputes between people or between people and the state. The legislature makes laws and the executive implements them.

question: Citizenship is best defined as a member of a state who is legally and constitutionally
solution: Citizenship is best defined as a member of a state who is legally and constitutionally recognised. A citizen has rights and duties in the state, and the law accepts him as a member. Being established, associated or united does not capture the legal meaning.

question: The Nigerian military cited which of the reasons for taking over the government in the country?

option.a: poor funding of military operations and a lack of allocation
option.b: mismanagement of public funds by the elected political leaders
option.c: intervention of foreign nations in Nigeria's politics and public fund
option.d: lack of credible political leaders and political party system

solution: The Nigerian military cited mismanagement of public funds by elected political leaders as a reason for taking over government. In the 1966 coup, soldiers complained about corruption, election violence and bad governance. Poor funding, foreign intervention and weak leadership were not the main reason given.

question: The two constitutions that provided for the election of four legislative members were
solution: The two constitutions that provided for the election of four legislative members were the Clifford and Richards constitutions. Clifford introduced the elective principle with elected members, and Richards continued and expanded it. The Macpherson and Lyttleton constitutions came later with different arrangements.

question: Nigeria gained independence in
solution: Nigeria gained independence in 1960. On 1 October 1960 the country became independent of British rule, with Tafawa Balewa as Prime Minister. The year 1963 is when Nigeria became a republic, 1957 was when internal self-government began in the regions, and 1979 was the start of the Second Republic.

question: Nigeria became a republic in
solution: Nigeria became a republic in 1963. The 1963 Republican Constitution removed the Queen as Head of State and replaced her with a Nigerian President, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe. The country was already independent in 1960, and 1979 and 1999 were later constitutional changes.

question: The first military coup in Nigeria occurred in
solution: The first military coup in Nigeria occurred in 1966. On 15 January 1966 soldiers led by Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu and others overthrew the civilian government. The other dates come before or after this event.

question: The 1999 Constitution established
solution: The 1999 Constitution established a presidential system of government. It created an executive President who is both Head of State and Head of Government, with a separate legislature and judiciary. The parliamentary system was used before 1966, and Nigeria is not a monarchy or a unitary state.

question: INEC is responsible for
solution: INEC, the Independent National Electoral Commission, is responsible for conducting elections. It registers voters and political parties, organises polls and announces results. Law enforcement belongs to the police, revenue collection to the revenue agencies, and foreign affairs to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

question: The Supreme Court is the
solution: The Supreme Court is the highest court in Nigeria. It is the final court of appeal, and its decisions bind all other courts in the country. It is not the lowest court, and it is not a military tribunal.

question: The doctrine of checks and balances prevents
solution: The doctrine of checks and balances prevents abuse of power. Each arm of government can check the others, so no single arm becomes too powerful. For example, the legislature can refuse to approve a budget, and the courts can declare an action unconstitutional. It does not prevent elections or the constitution.

question: Amnesty International is a
solution: Amnesty International is an international non-governmental organisation (NGO). It campaigns peacefully for human rights around the world and is not part of any government. It is not a political party or a military alliance.

question: A manifesto contains
solution: A manifesto contains a political party's policies and programmes. It explains what the party promises to do if it wins power, such as improving education or creating jobs. Court judgments, military orders and the constitution are not manifestos.

question: Good governance includes
solution: Good governance includes transparency. A good government lets citizens see how decisions are made and how public money is spent. Corruption, dictatorship and censorship are the opposite of good governance.

question: The pre-colonial political system of the Hausa-Fulani was mainly
solution: The pre-colonial political system of the Hausa-Fulani was mainly a centralised emirate system. Each emirate was ruled by an Emir with district heads and officials under him. It was not acephalous, republican or a simple democratic monarchy.

question: The Oyo Empire operated a system of
solution: The Oyo Empire operated a system of constitutional monarchy with checks. The Alaafin was the king, but the Oyomesi council could advise him and even ask him to abdicate, while the Ogboni cult also checked his power. It was not an absolute monarchy or a military dictatorship.

question: The Igbo traditional system was largely
solution: The Igbo traditional system was largely acephalous. This means it had no single supreme ruler; families, villages, age grades and title societies shared authority. It was not centralised, feudal or monarchical like some other Nigerian societies.

question: Indirect Rule in Nigeria was introduced by
solution: Indirect Rule in Nigeria was introduced by Lord Lugard. He used existing traditional rulers and institutions to administer the people under British supervision, first in Northern Nigeria and later elsewhere. Herbert Macaulay and Nnamdi Azikiwe were nationalists, and Tafawa Balewa was a politician, not the author of indirect rule.

question: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 introduced
solution: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 introduced the elective principle in Nigeria. It allowed a few Africans to be elected to the Legislative Council, which was the first use of elections in the country. It did not introduce federalism, republicanism or universal suffrage.

question: The Richards Constitution of 1946 aimed to
solution: The Richards Constitution of 1946 aimed to promote regionalism. It divided Nigeria into three regions — North, West and East — each with its own house of assembly. It did not abolish traditional rulers, introduce military rule or establish a republic.

question: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 is noted for
solution: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 is noted for wide consultation. Drafts were discussed in villages, towns and regions before the constitution was made, which made it more acceptable to Nigerians. It did not lack consultation, and it did not abolish the regions.

question: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 established
solution: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 established a federal system in Nigeria. It shared powers between the central government and the regions and made the regions stronger. It did not create a unitary, monarchical or confederal system.

question: Nigeria became a federation officially in
solution: Nigeria became a federation officially in 1954. The Lyttleton Constitution of that year firmly established the federal arrangement between the central government and the regions. The years 1946 and 1951 were earlier constitutional steps, and 1960 was independence.

question: The first Governor-General of independent Nigeria was
solution: The first Governor-General of independent Nigeria was Nnamdi Azikiwe. At independence in 1960 he represented the Queen as Governor-General, while Tafawa Balewa was Prime Minister. Obafemi Awolowo and Yakubu Gowon held other offices.

question: The first Executive President of Nigeria was
solution: The first Executive President of Nigeria was Shehu Shagari. He took office in 1979 under the 1979 Constitution, which created an executive presidency for the first time. Nnamdi Azikiwe had been a ceremonial President, while Obasanjo and Babangida were military rulers.

question: The Nigerian Civil War lasted from
solution: The Nigerian Civil War lasted from 1967 to 1970. It began in July 1967 when the Eastern Region declared independence as Biafra and ended in January 1970 with the region's surrender. The other date ranges are incorrect.

question: The policy of Reconciliation, Reconstruction and Rehabilitation was introduced by
solution: The policy of Reconciliation, Reconstruction and Rehabilitation was introduced by Yakubu Gowon. After the civil war, his government tried to heal wounds, rebuild damaged infrastructure and resettle people. Murtala Mohammed, Obasanjo and Buhari led later governments.

question: The 1979 Constitution introduced
solution: The 1979 Constitution introduced the presidential system in Nigeria. It created an executive President elected by the people, with a clear separation of powers between the executive, legislature and judiciary. The parliamentary system had been used in the First Republic.

question: The Federal Character principle promotes
solution: The Federal Character principle promotes fair representation. It tries to ensure that appointments and government institutions reflect all parts of the country, so that no group is left out. It does not promote military balance, ethnic dominance or secession.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: Revenue allocation in Nigeria is handled mainly by
solution: Revenue allocation in Nigeria is handled mainly by the Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC). It calculates how the Federation Account is shared among the federal, state and local governments. INEC runs elections, EFCC fights corruption, and NPC conducts censuses.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: The doctrine of separation of powers ensures
solution: The doctrine of separation of powers ensures specialisation of functions. Each arm of government concentrates on its own job: the legislature makes laws, the executive implements them and the judiciary interprets them. It does not concentrate or fuse power, and it has nothing to do with military control.

question: Delegated legislation is also known as
solution: Delegated legislation is also known as executive legislation. It is law made by bodies such as ministers, local governments or public corporations under powers given by an Act of Parliament. It is not primary legislation, judicial review or a party manifesto.

question: Public corporations are established to
solution: Public corporations are established to provide essential services. They supply water, electricity, transport and similar services that people need, often where private business would not provide them at a fair price. They are not set up to make private profit, contest elections or conduct referenda.

question: The ombudsman investigates
solution: The ombudsman investigates administrative injustice. In Nigeria the Public Complaints Commission performs this role by looking into complaints about unfair treatment by government officials. It does not investigate electoral fraud, military crimes or party disputes.

question: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in
solution: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in 1948. The United Nations General Assembly adopted it on 10 December 1948, and that date is now marked as Human Rights Day. The UN itself was formed in 1945.

question: Non-alignment means
solution: Non-alignment means neutrality in power blocs. A non-aligned country refuses to join either of the rival camps in a conflict, such as the Western and Eastern blocs during the Cold War. It does not mean a military alliance, economic dependency or colonial rule.

question: The Cold War involved rivalry between
solution: The Cold War involved rivalry between the USA and the USSR. After the Second World War, the United States and the Soviet Union competed for influence around the world without fighting each other directly. The other pairs were not the main rivals in the Cold War.

question: The African Union replaced
solution: The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity (OAU). The OAU was founded in 1963 and was replaced by the African Union in 2002 to give the continent a stronger and more united body. ECOWAS, the UN and the Commonwealth are different organisations.

question: ECOWAS was established in
solution: ECOWAS was established in 1975. The Treaty of Lagos was signed on 28 May 1975 by fifteen West African states to promote economic integration. The other dates are not correct.

question: The Commonwealth is mainly composed of
solution: The Commonwealth is mainly composed of former British colonies. It began as a group of countries that had been ruled by Britain and chose to keep links with one another. It is not made up mainly of French colonies, military states or socialist states.

question: Bicameralism at state level in Nigeria exists in
solution: Bicameralism at state level in Nigeria exists in none of the states. All state Houses of Assembly in Nigeria are unicameral, with only one chamber. Bicameralism exists at the federal level, where there is a Senate and a House of Representatives.

question: Judicial independence is secured mainly by
solution: Judicial independence is secured mainly by security of tenure. Judges cannot be removed easily; a special procedure is required, so they can decide cases without fear of losing their jobs. Executive control, political pressure and party loyalty would weaken judicial independence, not protect it.

question: A vote of no confidence is common in
solution: A vote of no confidence is common in a parliamentary system. If parliament passes a vote of no confidence in the Prime Minister or cabinet, the government must resign or call an election. A presidential system separates the executive from the legislature, so this device is not used in the same way.

question: Public accountability requires
solution: Public accountability requires transparency. Public officials must explain their actions and show how public money is used, so that citizens can hold them responsible. Secrecy, dictatorship and military rule are the opposite of accountability.

question: Nation-state is synonymous with
solution: A nation-state is a country whose people share a common identity and live under one independent government. The idea of supreme and independent authority is captured by sovereignty. Self-actualization, liberation and nationalism describe feelings or movements, not the state itself.

question: A fundamental component of political culture is
solution: Political culture is the set of beliefs, attitudes and values that people hold about politics. The most basic of these are social values, because they shape how people judge what is right and wrong in public life. Family and economic values matter too, but political culture rests mainly on shared social values.

question: A form of oligarchy in which gifted people are at the helm of affairs is
solution: An aristocracy is a form of oligarchy in which the best or most gifted people rule. A plutocracy is rule by the rich, a theocracy is rule by religious leaders, and a gerontocracy is rule by old people. The gifted few therefore point to aristocracy.

question: A state that is ruled by an elected citizen is
solution: A republic is a state headed by an elected citizen rather than a hereditary ruler. In a monarchy the ruler inherits the throne, a plutocracy is run by the wealthy, and an empire is a group of territories under one supreme ruler. An elected leader is what makes a state a republic.

question: A true democracy in the modern sense exists where the
solution: In the modern world, true democracy is representative: the people choose leaders who rule on their behalf. That is why democracy exists where elected representatives rule. Direct rule by all the people is not how modern states work in practice.

question: In a parliamentary system, when the legislature passes a vote of no confidence on the executive it means that the

option.a: executive is expected to go on suspension
option.c: legislature ceases to trust the executive
option.d: legislature commences legal proceeding against the executive

solution: In a parliamentary system, the government is formed from the legislature and stays in office only while it keeps the confidence of parliament. If parliament passes a vote of no confidence, the executive is required to resign, or the prime minister may ask for parliament to be dissolved. So the executive is required to resign.

question: The legislative body of the United States of America is the
solution: The legislature of the United States is called Congress. It has two chambers: the Senate and the House of Representatives. Parliament is the British legislature, while National Assembly is used in Nigeria and France.

question: The upper house in most federal systems is created to

option.b: oversee and check  the lower house
option.d: enable experienced elders make inputs to governance

solution: In a federation, the upper house (such as the Senate) is created mainly to give each state or region equal representation, so that all federating units are treated equally no matter their size. It is not designed to prevent executive excesses; that is the work of checks and balances.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: In which of the following systems is the power of the component units more than that of the central government?
solution: In a confederation, the component states keep most of the power and the central government only has the powers the states give it. In a federation power is shared, and in a unitary system the centre is strongest. So the confederal system gives the units more power than the centre.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: One of the general tenets of fascists doctrine is that a leader is

option.b: surbodinate to the laws of the state
option.d: surbodinate to the norms of the society

solution: Fascism teaches that the leader stands above the law and the constitution. The leader is seen as the voice of the nation, so his will is supreme relative to the constitution. This is the opposite of democracy, where everyone, including leaders, is subject to the law.

question: In a cabinet system of government, executive power is exercised by the
solution: In a cabinet system (also called parliamentary government), executive power is exercised by the head of government, usually a prime minister, together with the cabinet. The president or monarch is only a ceremonial head of state. So the head of government is the correct answer.

question: The principle of separation of powers is best practiced in the
solution: The principle of separation of powers divides government into three arms: legislature, executive and judiciary. It is best practised in a presidential system, where the president is not a member of the legislature and each arm checks the others. In a parliamentary system the executive and legislature are fused.

question: A typical form of delegated legislation is
solution: Delegated legislation is law made by a body other than the legislature, using powers the legislature has given it. A bye-law made by a local council or public body is a typical example. An act is made by the legislature, a decree by a military government, and a bill is only a proposal.

question: The rights of a citizen can be withdrawn by the state if the person

option.b: is convicted of a serious crime

solution: Citizenship rights are not absolute. The state can withdraw a person's rights when that person is convicted of a serious crime, because the law must protect the wider society. Disagreeing with the government, travelling abroad or listening to rumour is not enough to lose citizenship.

question: An electoral process in which candidates are selected for elective offices by party members is
solution: A primary election is the process in which party members choose the candidate who will represent the party in the main election. A general election is when all voters choose office holders, a bye-election fills one vacant seat, and an electoral college is a group of electors. So the answer is primary election.

question: In theory, one major advantage of the one-party system is that it

option.b: promotes greater mass participation in government
option.c: serves as an instrument of national integration

solution: In theory, a one-party system can be praised for national integration: everyone belongs to the same party, so tribal and regional divisions may be reduced. It does not guarantee social justice or greater mass participation; in fact it often limits them. That is why integration is the advantage usually claimed.

question: A tactic employed by pressure groups to achieve their objectives is
solution: Lobbying is the direct persuasion of lawmakers and government officials by pressure groups. Group members meet legislators, send memoranda and argue their case so that decisions favour them. Electioneering campaigns belong to political parties, while propaganda is only one tool of persuasion.

question: Public opinion can be measured through
solution: Public opinion is what most people think about an issue. It can be measured by asking the people to vote on a specific question, and that is what a referendum does. Negotiation, strike action and rumour are not reliable ways of measuring opinion.

question: Which of the following is the main function of the civil service

option.c: Allocating resources to the federating units
option.d: Mobilizing grass root support for government

solution: The civil service is the permanent body of officials who carry out government decisions. Its main function is therefore implementing government policies. It is supposed to be neutral, so it does not campaign for a party or mobilise support for the government of the day.

question: Who was the political head of the Old Oyo Empire?
solution: The Alaafin was the political head of the Old Oyo Empire. He ruled with the Oyomesi, a council of chiefs led by the Bashorun, and the Aremo was the heir to the throne. So the Alaafin was the supreme political authority.

question: The Aro age-grade system in Igbo land was
solution: The Aro age-grade system in Igboland was a political organisation. Age grades took decisions, settled disputes and organised communal work, so they played a governing role in the community. They were not mainly religious or commercial bodies.

question: France introduced the policy of assimilation in her colonies primarily to

option.a: teach them the art of leadership

solution: France's policy of assimilation aimed to turn Africans into French people by changing their way of life: language, dress, religion and customs. It was not mainly about education or leadership training; the goal was cultural and political absorption into France.

question: The foremost British trading company on the West African coast was
solution: The United African Company was the foremost British trading company on the West African coast. It later became the Royal Niger Company, which received a charter to administer parts of the area. Lever Brothers and John Holt came later.

question: Which of these rulers resisted colonial rule and was deported to Calabar?
solution: Oba Ovoranwen of Benin resisted British colonial rule and was deported to Calabar in 1897 after the British invaded Benin City. King Jaja of Opobo was also deported, but to the West Indies. The question points to the Benin king.

question: One of the major weaknesses of the Independence constitution is that it

option.a: failed to provide the country with full sovereignty
option.b: gave full powers to the supreme Court in Nigeria
option.d: empowered Britain to continue to rule

solution: The Independence Constitution of 1960 still left important powers with Britain. For example, the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London remained the final court of appeal, so Nigeria did not have full sovereignty. Full independence in law came with the 1963 Republican Constitution.

question: The first law-making body in Nigeria after amalgamation was
solution: The first law-making body in Nigeria after the 1914 amalgamation was the Nigerian Council, created by Lord Lugard. It was largely advisory and had mostly appointed members. The Legislative Council came later, and the National Assembly belongs to the independence era.

question: The designation of ministers as chief executives and accounting officers was recommended by a commission headed by
solution: The Dotun Phillips Commission (1985) recommended that ministers be chief executives and accounting officers of their ministries. This was implemented in the 1988 civil service reforms. The Udoji Commission dealt with pay and the structure of the public service, not this specific change.

question: A major shortcoming of the Ombudsman is

option.b: its inability to restrain bureaucratic excesses
option.d: lack of executive power to enforce decisions

solution: The Ombudsman (Public Complaints Commission) investigates complaints of unfair treatment by officials. Its main weakness is that it has no executive power to enforce its decisions; it can only recommend. That limits how far it can correct administrative injustice.

question: One of the strong points of the multiparty system in Nigeria's Fourth Republic is

option.a: the provision for a bicameral legislature

solution: A multiparty system allows many parties to compete, so more groups and opinions are represented. In Nigeria's Fourth Republic this has widened political participation. It does not remove government interference, and it certainly does not encourage anti-democracy campaigns.
category: Political Parties and Party Politics in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: In which of the following is the ceremonial and executive powers fused?
solution: In a presidential system, one person, the president, is both the ceremonial head of state and the chief executive. The two roles are therefore fused in the same office. In a parliamentary system they are separated between a ceremonial head and a prime minister.

question: A major contentious issue confronting the Nigerian Federalism is
solution: The biggest contentious issue in Nigerian federalism is revenue allocation: how money from the federation account is shared among the federal, state and local governments. States often argue about the formula and about resource control. Poverty, health and education are problems, but they are not the main constitutional dispute.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: The main purpose of establishing public enterprise in Nigeria is to
solution: Public enterprises are set up mainly to provide essential services that private business may not provide at a fair price, such as water, electricity and transport. Making profit is not their main aim, and they are not created to compete with private firms.

question: Parastatals are established to
solution: Parastatals are government-owned bodies created to render social services to the people. They provide services like power, water, broadcasting and transport. Profit maximisation is secondary, and they are not training grounds for entrepreneurs.

question: The General Purpose Committee of the local government is

option.b: body responsible for supervising self-help projects

solution: The General Purpose Committee of a local government works like the cabinet of the local government. It brings together the chairman and supervisors to discuss and take decisions on local matters. It is not just a public relations unit or a contract-awarding body.

question: The highest organ of the state during Babangida Regime was the
solution: During the Babangida regime, the highest ruling body was the Armed Forces Ruling Council (AFRC). Babangida later replaced it with the Provisional Ruling Council (PRC). The Supreme Military Council belonged to earlier regimes, and the Federal Executive Council is a civilian body.

question: Decree 34 of 1966 was unacceptable to many Nigerians because it was

option.a: seen as an instrument of impoverishment
option.b: promulgated without consultation with the people
option.c: perceived to abolish the federal system

solution: Decree 34 of 1966 (the Unification Decree) tried to turn Nigeria into a unitary state by removing the regions. Many Nigerians saw it as an attempt to abolish the federal system, and it increased tension before the civil war. It was not rejected mainly because of consultation.

question: Nigeria broke diplomatic relations with France in 1961 because

option.a: France's atomic test in the Sahara Desert
option.b: Her poor relations with the francophone countries
option.c: General de-Gaulle's negative attitude towards her

solution: Nigeria broke diplomatic relations with France in 1961 because France carried out an atomic test in the Sahara Desert. Nigeria protested that the test endangered Africans and showed disregard for the continent. The other options are not the recorded reason.

question: An attribute that Nigeria shares with most non-aligned countries is
solution: The non-aligned movement was made up mostly of developing countries that refused to join either the Western or the Eastern bloc. What Nigeria shares with most of them is the state of her economy: a developing economy that needed aid from both sides. Large size or population is not shared by all members.

question: Nigeria spearheaded the formation of ECOWAS during the regime of
solution: Nigeria spearheaded the formation of ECOWAS during the regime of General Yakubu Gowon. The treaty was signed in Lagos in 1975. Obasanjo and Murtala Muhammed came later, and Babangida after them.

question: Nigeria was classified as a front line state for

option.a: participating in a peacekeeping in the Congo
option.b: spearheading the formation of African Union
option.c: supporting the liberation efforts in Southern Africa
option.d: helping to end the crisis in Liberia

solution: A frontline state was a country that actively supported the struggle to end colonial and white-minority rule in Southern Africa. Nigeria earned the name by supporting liberation efforts in Southern Africa, including the fight against apartheid. Peacekeeping in Congo or Liberia is not what the term means.

question: The development of attitudes and beliefs about a political system is
solution: Political socialisation is the lifelong process through which people learn the attitudes, beliefs and values of their political system. Family, school, peer groups and the mass media all teach these attitudes. Political participation is taking part in politics, not learning about it.

question: Political behavior is governed by
solution: Political culture is the pattern of beliefs, values and attitudes that guides how people behave in politics. Because it shapes what people expect and accept, it governs political behaviour. Political ideology is only one part of that wider culture.

question: In a nation, sovereignty is vested in the
solution: Sovereignty is the supreme power to make and enforce laws. In a nation, that power belongs to the state, which is the organised political community. The community, elite and electorate may influence decisions, but the state is where sovereign power is vested.

question: Which of the following is a feature of democracy?
solution: A key feature of democracy is popular consultation: the government listens to the people through elections, referendums and public debate before taking major decisions. Interdependence of states is not a feature of democracy, and power is not vested in minority parties.

question: Private ownership of the means of production is central to
solution: Capitalism is built on private ownership of the means of production: land, factories and businesses belong to individuals, not the state. Fascism and feudalism also allow private property, but capitalism is the system defined by it. Communism calls for common ownership.

question: A system based on hierarchies of land ownership is
solution: Feudalism is a system based on hierarchies of land ownership. A lord gave land to lesser lords and knights in return for loyalty and service, while peasants worked the land. Totalitarianism, communism and fascism are modern systems, not land-based hierarchies.

question: Which of the following performs quasi-legislative functions?
solution: The executive performs quasi-legislative functions when it makes delegated legislation, such as rules, regulations and orders, under powers given by parliament. The judiciary interprets laws, the civil service implements them, and traditional institutions have no law-making power.

question: A major weakness of confederation is
solution: The major weakness of a confederation is its tendency towards secession. Because the component states keep most of their power and may leave when they disagree with the centre, the union is weak and can break up. It does not concentrate authority; it lacks it.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: Members of a parliament are required to report the proceedings of the house to their
solution: Parliamentarians represent the people of their constituencies. They are expected to report the proceedings of the house back to the voters and to present the constituency's views in parliament. Local government chairmen and traditional rulers are not their constituents.

question: Which of the following is a unitary state?
solution: Ghana is a unitary state: the central government holds the main powers and may create or dissolve local authorities. Nigeria, India and the United States are federal states, where power is shared between the centre and the states.

question: Ending a session of parliament by royal proclamation means the
solution: Prorogation is the ending of a parliamentary session by royal proclamation. Parliament is not dissolved; it simply stops sitting until the next session. Dissolution ends the life of parliament and is followed by a general election.

question: A main feature of the parliamentary system is that

option.a: the executive consists of all party members
option.b: judges are drawn from the ruling party
option.c: electoral commissioners leave at the end of their tenure
option.d: the executive is appointed by the legislature

solution: A main feature of the parliamentary system is that the executive is appointed by the legislature. The prime minister and ministers come from parliament and remain responsible to it. This is different from a presidential system, where the president is elected separately.

question: In a socialist economy,private accumulation of wealth is
solution: In a socialist economy, the means of production belong mainly to the state or the community, so private accumulation of wealth is prohibited or strictly controlled. The aim is to reduce inequality and provide for everyone. Regulating or limiting wealth is not enough; socialism opposes private accumulation itself.

question: The earliest classification of constitutions was the work of
solution: Aristotle made the earliest classification of constitutions. He grouped them into correct forms (monarchy, aristocracy, polity) and perverted forms (tyranny, oligarchy, democracy). Plato, Rousseau and Wheare wrote about government, but not this classification.

question: Constitutionalism refers to

option.a: the process of drafting a constitution
option.c: the process of operating a constitution

solution: Constitutionalism means strict adherence to a constitution: the government must act within the limits set by the constitution and no one is above the law. It is not just drafting or amending a constitution, but actually obeying it.

question: An advantage of delegated legislation is that

option.a: much time is saved in the process
option.b: technical issues are handled by experts
option.d: it hastens the implementation of policy

solution: Delegated legislation allows parliament to hand some law-making power to experts, such as ministers and technical bodies. A major advantage is that technical issues are handled by experts who understand the subject better than ordinary legislators. Saving time is also useful, but the special value of delegation is expert knowledge.

question: One essential duty of a citizen to his state is to
solution: Every citizen has duties to the state, and one essential duty is to pay taxes. Taxes provide the money government uses to build roads, schools and hospitals and to pay workers. Supporting the party in power is not a duty, because citizens may support any party.

question: Franchise in an electoral process means the

option.d: rights and duties of a citizen

solution: Franchise means the right to vote in elections. A person who has franchise is qualified to choose leaders at the polls. It is not about owning property or about the general rights and duties of citizenship.

question: The type of party system in practice is defined by the

option.a: relationship between the parties and electorate
option.c: manner in which the parties operate
option.d: number of political parties in a country

solution: The type of party system is defined by the number of political parties in a country. One party gives a one-party system, two main parties give a two-party system, and many parties give a multiparty system. How the parties operate is a different matter.

question: Pressure groups harmonize different individual concerns through
solution: Pressure groups bring together many separate demands and combine them into a few clear positions that they present to government. This process is called interest aggregation. Interest formulation and mobilisation are earlier steps, but aggregation is the combining of interests.

question: Opinion polls are organized to find out the

option.a: benefits derived by people from government
option.b: people's thought about a particular government policy
option.d: feelings of people about particular issues and policies

solution: Opinion polls are organised to find out the feelings of people about particular issues and policies. Pollsters ask a sample of people questions and use the answers to estimate what the wider public thinks. They are not mainly about benefits or expectations.

question: In pre-colonial Igboland, autocratic rule was made difficult by the

option.b: absence of a centralized system of authority

solution: In pre-colonial Igboland, autocratic rule was difficult because there was no centralised system of authority. Power was shared among village assemblies, age grades and title societies, so no single ruler could control everyone. This is why Igbo society is called acephalous.

question: The Yoruba traditional system of government was
solution: The Yoruba traditional system of government was monarchical. Each kingdom had a king, such as the Alaafin of Oyo or the Ooni of Ife, who ruled with a council of chiefs. It was not a republic, and it was not fully democratic or egalitarian.

question: Under the pre-colonial Sokoto Caliphate system, the next in command to the sultan was the
solution: In the pre-colonial Sokoto Caliphate, the Waziri was next in command to the Sultan. He served as the chief adviser and head of the administration. The Galadima and Madaki were also senior officials, but the Waziri ranked highest.

question: Which of the following societies was classified as acephalous?
solution: An acephalous society is one without a centralised head or king. Pre-colonial Igbo society fits this description, because decisions were taken by village assemblies, councils of elders and age grades. Benin had a king, and the Ibibio and Ijaw had their own chiefly structures.

question: Indirect rule encouraged
solution: Indirect rule relied on traditional rulers and created warrant chiefs, native courts and native authorities. It also produced a class of educated Nigerians and exposed the injustices of colonial rule, so it encouraged the rise of nationalism. Exploitation certainly occurred, but the question asks for the political effect.

question: The main achievement of the nationalists in Nigeria was
solution: The main achievement of Nigerian nationalists was the political liberation of the nation. Through protests, newspapers, petitions and political parties, they won independence from British rule in 1960. Economic liberation and nation-building came later and were not their main achievement.

question: The major external factor that promoted nationalism in Nigeria was
solution: The Second World War was the major external factor that promoted nationalism in Nigeria. The war weakened Britain and other colonial powers, exposed the hypocrisy of fighting for freedom abroad while ruling colonies at home, and spread ideas of self-determination. Pan-Africanism also helped, but the war had the greater impact.

question: The presidential system of government was introduced in Nigeria with the Constitution of
solution: The presidential system of government was introduced in Nigeria by the 1979 Constitution. It created an executive president who was elected separately from the legislature. The 1960 and 1963 constitutions used a parliamentary system.

question: The Action Group crisis of 1963 led to the formation of
solution: The Action Group crisis of 1963 split the party and led to the formation of the United People's Party (UPP) by Chief Samuel Akintola and his followers. NEPU, NPC and NCNC were older parties that already existed.

question: Under the 1963 Republican Constitution, the power of judicial review was vested in the
solution: Under the 1963 Republican Constitution, the power of judicial review belonged to the Supreme Court. It could declare laws or actions unconstitutional. The President and Parliament could not review the constitutionality of laws.

question: The rules and regulations of the civil service are called?
solution: The rules and regulations of the civil service are called the General Order. They set out how civil servants are recruited, promoted, disciplined and paid. Bureaucratic, service and administrative orders are not the recognised name.

question: The Code of Conduct Bureau was essentially established to

option.b: protect the rights of public servants
option.c: enhance probity and accountability in public service
option.d: ensure the independence of the public service

solution: The Code of Conduct Bureau was established to enhance probity and accountability in public service. It receives asset declarations from public officers and checks abuse of office. Reducing corruption is the general aim, but probity and accountability is the precise duty.

question: Which of the following political parties was the first to be formed when the ban on politics was lifted in 1978?
solution: When the ban on politics was lifted in 1978, the Unity Party of Nigeria (UPN) was the first party to be formed. It was led by Chief Obafemi Awolowo. The NPN, NPP and PRP followed later.

question: The principle of federal character was adopted in order to promote equitable allocation of

option.a: positions and appointments among people of various regions
option.b: appointments between the North and the South
option.c: opportunities between the males and females
option.d: revenue between groups in the country

solution: The federal character principle was adopted to ensure equitable allocation of positions and appointments among people of various regions. It aims to make every part of the country feel represented in federal institutions. It is not mainly about revenue or gender.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: The component units of the Nigerian Federation comprises

option.c: federal,state,local government and federal capital territory
option.d: federal capital territory,national assembly,supreme court and civil service

solution: The component units of the Nigerian Federation are the federal, state and local governments, together with the Federal Capital Territory. These are the levels and units through which power is shared. The military, police and civil service are institutions, not component units.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: In Nigeria, privatization and commercialization policies were introduced to

option.a: hand over the control of commercial ventures to citizens
option.b: increase the asset base of government
option.c: divest government major control of commercial ventures
option.d: allow government control of the private sector

solution: Privatisation and commercialisation were introduced to divest government of major control of commercial ventures. The aim was to sell or reduce government shares in businesses so that private investors could run them more efficiently. It was not meant to increase government assets or control the private sector.

question: An example of a public corporation in Nigeria is
solution: The Nigerian Television Authority (NTA) is an example of a public corporation. It is owned by the government and provides a public service. The National Universities Commission and National Population Commission are commissions, while First Bank is a private commercial bank.

question: Following the reform of the Native Authority system in Northern Nigeria ,traditional rulers became
solution: After the reform of the Native Authority system in Northern Nigeria, traditional rulers became Chief-in-Council. The ruler now had to act with the advice and consent of a council, rather than alone. This reduced the absolute power of the chiefs.

question: Under whose regime were Akwa Ibom and Katsina States created?
solution: Akwa Ibom and Katsina States were created in 1987 under the regime of General Ibrahim Babangida. Babangida created several states during his tenure. Murtala Muhammed, Abacha and Gowon created other states at different times.

question: The distinctive attribute of a state is the monopoly of
solution: The distinctive attribute of a state is its monopoly of violence, meaning the lawful use of force. Only the state can legally keep an army, police and prisons, and it uses them to enforce its laws. Other groups may have power, but only the state may use force lawfully.

question: State as a political entity refers to

option.a: An organized group within a definite territory
option.b: An association of men in a given society

solution: A state is an organised group of people living within a definite territory, with a government and sovereignty. An association of men in a society is too loose, and a geographical location is only a place. The organised community with a government makes it a state.

question: Political values are acquired in any given society through
solution: Political values are learned, not inborn. They are acquired through political socialisation, the process by which family, school, religion, peers and the mass media teach people what to believe about politics. Re-orientation and campaigns only reinforce what has already been learned.

question: In a democratic government, political sovereignty is vested in the
solution: In a democracy, political sovereignty belongs to the electorate, the body of citizens who vote. Leaders only exercise power because the people chose them, and they can be voted out. The legislature, executive and elite hold office, but the people are the final source of authority.

question: One judicial function performed by the executive is
solution: One judicial function performed by the executive is the granting of amnesty, a pardon that forgives offences. This is part of the prerogative of mercy held by the president or governor. Implementing court orders and appointing judges are also executive acts, but amnesty is the clearest judicial-type power.

question: A political system which empowers the leader with the ultimate responsibility to execute laws is
solution: Presidentialism is the political system in which the president is both head of state and head of government, with the ultimate responsibility to execute laws. Parliamentarianism gives that role to a prime minister and cabinet, while dictatorship and autocracy are not systems of responsible government.

question: A bill is a draft which is awaiting the consideration of the
solution: A bill is a draft law waiting for the consideration of the legislature. It becomes an act only after the legislature debates, amends and passes it and the executive assents. The executive, party caucus and judiciary do not pass bills.

question: The private ownership of the means of production is a feature of
solution: Capitalism is the system in which the means of production are privately owned. Individuals and companies own factories, land and businesses and keep the profits. Socialism and communism call for public ownership, and communalism is a small-scale sharing system.

question: In a feudal system, the two major classes are the serfs and the
solution: In a feudal system, the two major classes are the serfs and the lords. The lords owned the land and the serfs worked it in return for protection. Vassals were lesser nobles, not the main working class.

question: An example of a country with a flexible constitution is
solution: Britain has a flexible constitution because it is largely unwritten and can be changed by ordinary Acts of Parliament. The United States, South Africa and Benin Republic have written, rigid constitutions that need special procedures to amend.

question: The rule of law is negation of
solution: The rule of law means that the law is supreme and everyone is equal before it. It is therefore the negation of absolute power, because no ruler may act above the law. Equality before the law and limited power are parts of the rule of law, not its opposite.

question: To ensure the rights and freedom of citizens, the powers of the arms of government must be
solution: To protect the rights and freedom of citizens, the powers of the three arms of government must be separated. When legislature, executive and judiciary each have their own powers, they can check one another and no single arm can become too strong.

question: Delegated legislation is made by bodies other than the
solution: Delegated legislation is law made by bodies other than parliament, using powers parliament has given them. Ministers, local councils and public bodies may make rules and bye-laws. The president, governor and judiciary do not make delegated legislation in this sense.

question: The primary aim of pressure groups is to
solution: The primary aim of pressure groups is to protect the interest of members by influencing government decisions. They do not seek to capture political power, which is the aim of political parties. Attracting attention and fighting corruption may happen, but they are not the main purpose.

question: The French colonial system was underlined by the policy of
solution: The French colonial system was built on the policy of assimilation. France tried to turn educated Africans into French citizens by teaching them French language, culture and law. Paternalism and indirect rule were used by other colonial powers, especially Britain.

question: Which of the following is used in gauging public opinion?
solution: The mass media are used in gauging public opinion. Newspapers, radio, television and the internet report and discuss what people think, and they also shape opinion. A constitution, a school or an electoral college is not a tool for measuring public opinion.

question: Colonization of Africa was mainly motivated by
solution: The colonisation of Africa was mainly motivated by economic reasons. European powers wanted raw materials, new markets and places to invest their surplus capital. Security, religion and culture played a part, but economic gain was the driving force.

question: The commission charged with the conduct of federal elections in Nigeria is
solution: The commission charged with conducting federal elections in Nigeria is the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). It registers voters and parties, conducts elections and announces results. NEC, FEDECO and NECON were earlier bodies that no longer conduct federal elections.

question: In the Hausa pre- colonial political system, a district was headed by
solution: In the pre-colonial Hausa political system, a district was headed by a Hakimi. He collected taxes and kept order under the emir. The dagaci headed a village, the alkali was a judge, and the waziri was the chief adviser.

question: Which of the following ensured the practice of democracy in the pre-colonial Yoruba political system?
solution: The pre-colonial Yoruba political system practised checks and balances. The Alaafin or Oba ruled with a council of chiefs, such as the Oyomesi, which could restrain him. This sharing and checking of power kept the ruler from becoming a tyrant.

question: An electoral system in which parties are assigned seats in the parliament commensurate to the number of votes polled is
solution: An electoral system in which parties receive seats in parliament in proportion to the votes they poll is proportional representation. A party with 40 percent of the votes gets about 40 percent of the seats. Absolute and simple majority systems award seats by constituency, not by share of votes.

question: The bringing of a session of a parliament to an end through royal proclamation is known as
solution: The bringing of a parliamentary session to an end by royal proclamation is prorogation. Parliament stops sitting but is not dissolved. Dissolution ends parliament completely, and a vote of no confidence is a decision against the government.

question: The right of citizens to participate in the affairs of government of their country is called
solution: The right of citizens to take part in the government of their country is a political right. It includes the right to vote, to contest elections and to hold public office. Economic, civil and social rights deal with money, personal freedom and welfare.

question: A permanent structure that facilitates continuity and guarantees orderly conduct in governance is
solution: A permanent structure that provides continuity and orderly conduct in governance is bureaucracy, the civil service. Officials keep records, apply rules and remain in office when governments change. Public corporations, the ombudsman and political parties come and go or serve other purposes.

question: An intra-party activity for the selection of candidates for elective positions is known as
solution: An intra-party activity for selecting candidates for elective positions is a primary election. Party members choose who will carry the party's flag in the general election. A general election is between parties, and a bye-election fills a single vacant seat.

question: Radical nationalism in Nigeria is generally attributed to the influence of
solution: Radical nationalism in Nigeria is generally attributed to the influence of Nnamdi Azikiwe. Through his newspaper, the West African Pilot, and the NCNC, he demanded self-government and stirred mass nationalist feeling. Herbert Macaulay founded the first party but was more moderate.

question: Two foreigners that directly aroused nationalist feelings among Nigerians are

option.c: W.E du Boise and H.O Davies

solution: Two foreigners who directly aroused nationalist feelings among Nigerians were Marcus Garvey and Casely Hayford. Garvey's Pan-African ideas and Hayford's West African nationalism inspired Nigerian leaders. The other pairs are either not foreign or not linked to Nigerian nationalism.

question: The Sharia legal system was first introduced in the Fourth Republic in
solution: The Sharia legal system was first introduced in the Fourth Republic in Zamfara State in 1999. Other northern states later followed. Kano, Katsina and Sokoto also adopted it, but Zamfara was the first.

question: The main focus of Nigeria's foreign policy since independence centers on
solution: Nigeria's foreign policy since independence has centred on Afrocentrism, often called Africa as the centrepiece. Nigeria gives priority to African unity, decolonisation and cooperation with African states. Sub-regionalism and globalism are parts of this wider African focus.

question: Military intervention in Nigeria arose from

option.a: perceived incapability of civilians to govern
option.c: the desire for a military government

solution: Military intervention in Nigeria arose mainly from the perceived incapability of civilians to govern. Soldiers claimed that politicians were corrupt, elections were rigged and order had broken down. International pressure and a desire for military rule were not the real causes.

question: The first institution introduced by the military to exercise legislative power was the
solution: The first institution introduced by the military to exercise legislative power was the Supreme Military Council. It made laws by decree after the 1966 coup. The Armed Forces Ruling Council and Provisional Ruling Council came later under Babangida and Abacha.

question: The central objective of privatization in Nigeria is to
solution: The central objective of privatisation in Nigeria is to improve the efficiency of enterprises. Government-owned firms were often poorly run, so selling them to private owners was expected to make them more productive. Reducing retrenchment or raising salaries was not the aim.

question: Workers in the public corporations are known as
solution: Workers in public corporations are known as public servants. They are employed by government-owned bodies such as the NTA or the ports authority. Civil servants work in ministries, while private employees work for private companies.

question: Quota system and federal character principles were entrenched in the 1979 constitution to ensure
solution: The quota system and federal character principles were entrenched in the 1979 Constitution to ensure equity. They aimed at fair representation of all regions and groups in federal appointments and admissions. Loyalty, economic empowerment and even development were hoped-for results, but equity was the purpose.

question: In Nigeria, the agency mainly responsible for the maintenance of internal peace and security is the
solution: The agency mainly responsible for maintaining internal peace and security in Nigeria is the police. The Nigeria Police Force prevents crime, arrests offenders and keeps public order. The army, navy and civil defence have other roles, such as external defence and emergency support.

question: The National Assembly in Nigeria is primarily responsible for
solution: The National Assembly of Nigeria is primarily responsible for making laws. It debates and passes bills, represents the people and oversees the executive. Executing laws belongs to the executive, and interpreting them belongs to the courts.

question: The major factor militating against the efficient operation of electoral commissions in Nigeria is
solution: The major factor militating against the efficient operation of electoral commissions in Nigeria is excessive political interference. Politicians in power try to influence the commission's funding, appointments and results. Inadequate manpower and public support are problems, but political interference is the biggest.

question: A major objective of the public Complaints Commission is

option.a: Training and promotion of public servants
option.c: Addressing the grievances of individuals and groups

solution: A major objective of the Public Complaints Commission is addressing the grievances of individuals and groups against government officials. It investigates unfair treatment and recommends remedies. It does not train public servants, settle private disputes or fight corruption directly.

question: The country that championed decolonization in Africa was
solution: The country that championed decolonisation in Africa was Ghana. Under Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana became the first sub-Saharan colony to gain independence in 1957 and then supported liberation movements across Africa. Nigeria, South Africa and Kenya played roles, but Ghana led the way.

question: One of the programmes binding members of the Commonwealth is the
solution: One of the programmes binding members of the Commonwealth is the Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan. It funds students and researchers from member countries to study in one another's institutions. The Agenda for Peace is a United Nations document, not a Commonwealth programme.

question: Power that is delegated is exercised
solution: Delegated power is not exercised by the person who owns it but by someone else, so it is exercised indirectly. For example, parliament may delegate law-making to a minister, who then acts on parliament's behalf. Devolution, coercion and direct exercise describe other things.

question: De Jure sovereignty is acquired through
solution: De jure sovereignty is sovereignty that is legally acquired and recognised, so it comes through law. De facto sovereignty, by contrast, is based on actual control, such as by force or conquest. Treaty and grant can create rights, but legal sovereignty rests on law.

question: A group of people who live together under a common law within a definite territory is a
solution: A state is a group of people living together under a common law within a definite territory. It has a government and sovereignty. A community is smaller, a nation is a people with shared identity, and a nation-state combines both ideas.

question: Political socialization is associated with

option.a: Military take over of civilian government

solution: Political socialisation is the process of transmitting political values from one generation to another. Family, school, church, peers and the media teach people what to believe about politics. Military takeovers and transitions are events, not the socialisation process.

question: According to Aristotle, a form of government in which the few rule for the benefit of all is
solution: According to Aristotle, an aristocracy is rule by a few good people for the benefit of all. When the few rule for their own benefit, it becomes an oligarchy. Autocracy is rule by one person, and diarchy is rule by two.

question: Rule by the old people is known as
solution: Rule by old people is called gerontocracy. The word comes from the Greek word for old man. Monarchy is rule by a king, theocracy is rule by religious leaders, and feudalism is a land-based social system.

question: As an executive, the commissioner is charged with the responsibility of
solution: As an executive, a commissioner is charged with implementing laws. The commissioner heads a ministry and turns government policy into action. Writing and making laws belong to the legislature, and giving loans is not an executive function.

question: Rules adjudication is a primary function of the
solution: Rule adjudication, which means settling disputes and interpreting the law, is a primary function of the judiciary. Courts decide cases and explain what the law means. The executive implements laws, and the legislature makes them.

question: The judiciary controls the executive in federal state through
solution: The judiciary controls the executive in a federal state through judicial review. Courts can declare an action of the executive unconstitutional or illegal. Delegated legislation is made by the executive, and motions are used in the legislature.

question: One major advantage of the unitary system is that it tends to make government
solution: One major advantage of the unitary system is that it tends to make government strong and stable. Power is concentrated at the centre, so decisions are made quickly and applied uniformly. The system may be distant from the people, but that is a disadvantage, not an advantage.

question: The presidential system differs from the parliamentary system of government in that

option.a: The principle of collective responsibility applies
option.b: Executive and legislative powers are fused
option.c: Powers of the three arms of government are merged
option.d: The tenure of office of the president is limited

solution: The presidential system differs from the parliamentary system in that the tenure of office of the president is limited to a fixed term. The president does not depend on parliament's confidence and cannot be removed by a simple vote of no confidence. Collective responsibility and fusion of powers belong to the parliamentary system.

question: Which of the following advocates equitable distribution of wealth?
solution: Socialism advocates equitable distribution of wealth. It wants the state to own or control the main means of production so that wealth is shared more fairly. Capitalism allows wide inequality, while aristocracy and plutocracy are forms of rule by a few or by the rich.
