question: A constitution that is difficult to amend is
solution: A constitution that is difficult to amend is a rigid constitution. It usually requires a special majority or a referendum before it can be changed. A flexible constitution can be changed by an ordinary law, and written or unwritten describes its form, not how hard it is to amend.

question: Which of the following constitutions is more suitable for centralization of political power?
solution: A flexible constitution is more suitable for the centralisation of political power. Because it can be changed easily by the central legislature, power can be concentrated at the centre without the delay of special amendment procedures. A rigid written constitution usually limits and divides power.

question: Which of the following types of citizenship cannot be withdrawn?
solution: Citizenship by birth cannot normally be withdrawn. A person born a citizen holds that status as a right, even if they commit a crime. Citizenship by naturalisation or registration can be withdrawn in certain cases, and honorary citizenship is a gift that can be taken away.

question: The right of citizens to vote is
solution: The right of citizens to vote is called universal suffrage. It means that all adult citizens, regardless of sex, race or wealth, may vote. Nationality and adult suffrage are parts of the idea, but universal suffrage is the name for the general right.

question: A political party is different from a pressure group in its
solution: A political party differs from a pressure group mainly in its objective. A party wants to win elections and control government, while a pressure group only wants to influence government decisions. Organisation, strategy and finance may differ, but the aim is the key difference.

question: One of the functions of pressure groups is to

option.c: Articulate the opinion of their members
option.d: Contest elections to serve the people

solution: One function of pressure groups is to articulate the opinion of their members. They gather members' views and present them clearly to government and the public. They do not nominate the president, prepare the budget or contest elections in their own name.

question: Under the 1979 Constitution, statutory allocation of revenue to local government councils is the responsibility of the
solution: Under the 1979 Constitution, statutory allocation of revenue to local government councils was the responsibility of the Federal Legislature. The National Assembly made the law that set aside money for local governments from the federation account. State Houses of Assembly did not control this federal allocation.

question: Under Nigeria's Second Republic, the Senate was under the leadership of
solution: In Nigeria's Second Republic, the Senate was led by Joseph Wayas, who was Senate President from 1979 to 1983. J.S. Tarka and John Wash Pam were senators, and Godwin Ume-Ezeoke was Speaker of the House of Representatives.

question: The Revenue Mobilization, Allocation and Fiscal Commission is statutorily empowered to determine the remuneration of
solution: The Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission determines the remuneration of political office holders. This includes the president, governors, legislators and other elected or appointed officials. It does not fix the salaries of all civil servants or public corporation employees.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: The primary function of the Code of Conduct Bureau is to

option.d: Ensure due process by public officers

solution: The primary function of the Code of Conduct Bureau is to ensure a minimum standard of morality in public office. It receives asset declarations and checks that public officers do not abuse their positions. Receiving declarations is a means to that end, not the whole purpose.

question: The party system practiced in Nigeria's Third Republic was
solution: The party system practised in Nigeria's Third Republic was a two-party system. The military government created only two parties, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and the National Republican Convention (NRC). A multiparty system returned in the Fourth Republic.
category: Political Parties and Party Politics in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: Nigeria adopted the federal system of government because of

option.c: The adoption of a state religion
option.d: The fear of domination of minorities

solution: Nigeria adopted a federal system because of the fear of domination of minorities. Smaller ethnic groups feared being ruled by larger ones, so power was shared between the centre and the regions. Uneven development and limited resources were problems, not the main reason.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: The highest policy making body under the Gowon Regime was
solution: The highest policy-making body under the Gowon regime was the Supreme Military Council. It made laws and set major policies after the 1966 coup. The Armed Forces Ruling Council and Provisional Ruling Council came later under Babangida and Abacha.

question: Nigeria became a federation of thirty-six state during the era of
solution: Nigeria became a federation of thirty-six states during the era of Sani Abacha. In 1996 his government created six more states, bringing the total to thirty-six. Abdulsalami Abubakar and Babangida ruled at other times.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: Which of the following headed the committee that recommended the suitability of Abuja as a new federal city?
solution: Justice Akinola Aguda headed the committee that recommended Abuja as a suitable new federal capital. The committee was set up in the 1970s, and the capital later moved from Lagos to Abuja. The other justices served in different roles.

question: A public corporation is managed by
solution: A public corporation is managed by a board of directors. The board sets policy and supervises the management, while a general manager or managing director handles day-to-day running. A minister gives general policy guidelines but does not manage the corporation directly.

question: The provisional Ruling Council was the highest ruling body during the regime of
solution: The Provisional Ruling Council was the highest ruling body during the regime of Sani Abacha. Abacha replaced Babangida's Armed Forces Ruling Council with the PRC. Buhari and Murtala Muhammed ruled at other times.

question: Nigeria's non-alignment policy in the sixties lacked real substance because of her
solution: Nigeria's non-alignment policy in the 1960s lacked real substance because of her close ties with Britain. Although Nigeria claimed to be non-aligned, it still depended heavily on Britain for trade, defence and diplomacy. That made true neutrality difficult.

question: Under the Technical Aid Corps, Nigerian experts are deployed to

option.a: African, the pacific and the Caribbean
option.c: The pacific, the Caribbean and Europe

solution: Under the Technical Aid Corps, Nigerian experts are deployed to Africa, the Pacific and the Caribbean. The scheme sends doctors, teachers, engineers and other professionals to developing countries that need them. It does not send them mainly to Europe or Asia.

question: The center-piece of Nigeria's foreign policy covers only
solution: The centre-piece of Nigeria's foreign policy is Africa. Nigeria gives priority to African unity, peace and development, which is why the policy is often called Africa as the centrepiece. Europe, Latin America and Asia are important, but they are not the centre-piece.

question: Which of the following countries pioneered the establishment of ECOWAS alongside Nigeria?
solution: Togo pioneered the establishment of ECOWAS alongside Nigeria. President Gnassingbe Eyadema of Togo worked with Nigeria's General Gowon to promote the idea, and the treaty was signed in Lagos in 1975. Ghana, Algeria and Cameroon were not the co-founders.

question: Nigeria's role in the African Union was most prominent during the regime of
solution: Nigeria's role in the African Union was most prominent during the regime of President Olusegun Obasanjo. He served as AU chairman and pushed for African peacekeeping, debt relief and reform. Shagari, Yar'adua and Babangida led at other times.

question: A representative of a Commonwealth country in another member state is known as
solution: A representative of a Commonwealth country in another member state is known as a High Commissioner. Commonwealth countries exchange High Commissioners instead of ambassadors because they share a common head or history. Ambassador is used for non-Commonwealth countries.

question: The organ of UN that promotes voluntary co-operation among member states in diverse areas is the
solution: The UN organ that promotes voluntary cooperation among member states in many areas is the Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC). It deals with development, health, education and human rights. The General Assembly debates, the Security Council keeps peace, and the ICJ settles legal disputes.

question: The main representative body of the United Nations is the
solution: The main representative body of the United Nations is the General Assembly. Every member state has one vote there, and it discusses and approves the UN budget and major policies. The Security Council has greater enforcement power but fewer members.

question: The AU differs from the OAU in having

option.d: No assembly of Heads of State

solution: The African Union differs from the OAU in having effective tools for decision enforcement. The AU can suspend or sanction member states that break its rules, and it has a Peace and Security Council. The OAU relied more on persuasion and had weaker enforcement.

question: Under the emirate system, the commander of the army is the _____
solution: Under the emirate system, the commander of the army was the Madawaki. He led the emir's troops and defended the emirate. The Alkali was a judge, the Hakimi headed a district, and the Sarkin Fada was in charge of the palace.

question: The indirect rule system of administration was more successful in northern Nigeria because

option.a: the people were mainly interested in being governed indirectly
option.b: of the existence of an organized structure in the area
option.c: the Europeans ensured that the farmlands of the natives were not confisticated
option.d: the natives showed little or no resistance

solution: Indirect rule was more successful in northern Nigeria because of the existence of an organised structure in the area. The emirate system already had emirs, district heads and courts, so the British could rule through them. The South had no such centralised structure in many places.

question: The necessary attributes of a state are:

option.a: Definite territory  population, sovereingnty, and government

solution: The necessary attributes of a state are a definite territory, a population, sovereignty and a government. These four must all be present for a state to exist. A police force, army or immigration service is an agency of the state, not an essential attribute.

question: The process of taking part in political and public affairs can be termed political
solution: Taking part in political and public affairs is called political participation. It includes voting, joining a party, attending rallies and contesting elections. Political socialisation is learning about politics, not taking part in it.

question: Membership of a society is
solution: Membership of a society is voluntary. People choose to join or leave associations such as clubs, unions and pressure groups. A state, by contrast, is a compulsory community that a person belongs to by birth or law.

question: In a democratic political system, the political sovereign is usually the
solution: In a democratic political system, the political sovereign is usually the electorate. The people who vote are the final source of political authority, and leaders rule because the electorate chose them. The legislature and parties exercise power on the people's behalf.

question: One basic feature of a monarchical form of government is that

option.b: the ruler has a fixed tenure
option.d: members of the executive are elected

solution: One basic feature of a monarchical form of government is that succession is through heredity. The throne passes from one member of the royal family to another, usually from parent to child. A fixed tenure and elected executive belong to a republic or a democracy.

question: One main advantage of bicameral legislature is that it

option.a: is less cumbersome to pass bills
option.b: is not easy to manipulate bills
option.c: makes for quick deliberation during emergencies

solution: One main advantage of a bicameral legislature is that it is not easy to manipulate bills. A bill must pass through two chambers, so it is carefully examined and hasty or bad laws are harder to push through. It is slower and more cumbersome, not quicker.

question: The court that has unlimited power to interpreted the constitution is the
solution: The court with unlimited power to interpret the constitution is the Supreme Court. It is the highest court in the land, and its decisions on constitutional matters are final. The High Court and Court of Appeal are lower courts.

question: Unitary-system of government, is more suitable to a country

option.a: with a robust and dynamic economy
option.b: with a relatively small area and a homogenous population
option.d: that possesses a strong and moderm army

solution: A unitary system is more suitable for a country with a relatively small area and a homogenous population. With one central government and a similar people, decisions can be made and applied easily. Large, diverse countries usually prefer a federation.

question: An example of a country ruled by a constitutional monarch is
solution: Morocco is an example of a country ruled by a constitutional monarch. The king reigns within the limits of a constitution and an elected parliament. Italy, Libya and Uganda are republics, not constitutional monarchies.

question: The development of a classless society is the goal of
solution: The development of a classless society is the goal of Marxism. Marxists want to abolish private ownership of the means of production so that no exploiting class remains. Conservatism and feudalism preserve class differences, and liberalism accepts private property.

question: A flexible constitution is one which is
solution: A flexible constitution is one that is easily amended. It can be changed by an ordinary Act of Parliament, as in Britain. Being known to all or popular with legislators does not make a constitution flexible.

question: which of the following is a feature of checks and balances?
solution: A feature of checks and balances is judicial review. Courts can examine the actions of the legislature and executive and declare them unconstitutional. A code of conduct, judicial precedent and judicial immunity are legal rules, not the checking of one arm by another.

question: Laws made by military government at the state level are called
solution: Laws made by a military government at the state level are called edicts. Decrees are made at the federal level, while acts are made by a civilian legislature. Bye-laws are made by local authorities.

question: Citizenship is acquired by an alien through
solution: An alien can acquire Nigerian citizenship through registration. A person of full age who satisfies the constitutional conditions may apply to be registered as a citizen. Conferment and birth are not ways for an alien to acquire citizenship, and internalisation is not a legal term here.

question: The officer responsible, for announcing the result of an election is known as
solution: The officer responsible for announcing the result of an election is the returning officer. He or she declares the winner after the votes have been counted. Presiding officers run polling units, and ballot officers handle ballot papers.

question: The ultimate aim of political parties is to

option.a: increase the political awareness of the electorate

solution: The ultimate aim of political parties is to acquire and exercise power. Everything else, such as raising awareness or implementing programmes, follows from winning elections and forming government. Pressure groups, not parties, are content to influence power from outside.

question: The main objective of pressure groups is to

option.a: protect the interest of the country against foreigners
option.b: serve as opposition to the government
option.c: promote the interest of political parties
option.d: influence legislation for the benefit of their members

solution: The main objective of pressure groups is to influence legislation for the benefit of their members. They meet legislators, send memoranda and campaign to shape laws and policies. They do not seek to replace the government or promote parties.

question: Which of the following is not a dimension of public opinion?
solution: Polling is not a dimension of public opinion; it is a method of measuring it. The dimensions of public opinion include intensity (how strongly people feel) and orientation (which way they lean). Substance and polling are not dimensions in the standard list.

question: The body that is responsible for the appointment discipline, promotion and dismissal of civil servants
solution: The body responsible for the appointment, discipline, promotion and dismissal of civil servants is the Civil Service Commission. It handles personnel matters so that the service stays professional and politically neutral. A ministry of labour or establishment does not perform these duties.

question: In the per-colonial Hausa political system, the madawaki performed the function of
solution: In the pre-colonial Hausa political system, the Madawaki performed the function of Minister of Defence. He commanded the army and protected the state. The Alkali was a judge and the Hakimi headed a district.

question: In the Old Oyo Empire, the Ajele

option.a: was the one led by the army
option.b: ensured the safety of all trade routes
option.c: ensured good governance of the  districts

solution: In the Old Oyo Empire, the Ajele ensured good governance of the districts. The Alaafin sent Ajele officials to oversee the provinces and collect tribute. They represented the central authority in outlying areas.

question: The general Strike of 1945 was caused primarily by the

option.b: disparity in the criteria for employment
option.c: harshness in trade laws as it concerns the Africans
option.d: government's rejection of a demand for an increase of 50 percent in the cost of living allowances

solution: The general strike of 1945 was caused primarily by the government's rejection of a demand for an increase of 50 percent in the cost of living allowance. Workers had suffered under wartime inflation, and the refusal led to a nationwide strike. Discriminatory laws and trade rules were background grievances.

question: Before 1945, the component units of Nigeria were
solution: Before 1945, the component units of Nigeria were provinces. The country was divided into provinces under the colonial administration. Regions were created later, and states came after independence.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: The emergence of nationalism was essentially the result of the ills of
solution: The emergence of nationalism was essentially the result of the ills of colonialism. Colonial rule brought exploitation, discrimination and denial of political rights, and Nigerians organised to end it. Imperialism is the wider system, but colonialism is the direct experience that produced nationalism.

question: Which of the following nationalist was the founder of Nigeria's first political party
solution: Herbert Macaulay was the founder of Nigeria's first political party, the Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP), formed in 1923. Azikiwe, Balewa and Ahmadu Bello led later parties and movements.

question: The Nigeria Independence Constitution was modified by the
solution: The Nigeria Independence Constitution was modified by the 1963 Constitution. The 1963 Republican Constitution removed the Queen as head of state and made Nigeria a republic. The 1979, 1989 and 1999 constitutions came much later.

question: The president of Nigeria was indirectly elected through secret ballot for a period of five years by the senate in
solution: The president of Nigeria was indirectly elected through secret ballot for a period of five years by the Senate in 1963. Under the Republican Constitution, the president was chosen by the National Assembly. Direct election of the president began with the 1979 Constitution.

question: The main function of the federal character commission in Nigeria is

option.b: providing free social services to the citizens
option.c: ensuring fair representation of all states in the public service

solution: The main function of the Federal Character Commission is ensuring fair representation of all states in the public service. It monitors appointments and admissions so that no state or region is left out. It does not settle private disputes or provide social services.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: The power of appointing the chairman of the independent National Electoral commission is vested in the
solution: The power of appointing the chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission is vested in the President, subject to confirmation by the Senate. The president nominates, and the Senate approves. The commission itself does not appoint its chairman.

question: The NCNC and the NPC facilitated the creation of the
solution: The NCNC and the NPC facilitated the creation of the Mid-West Region in 1963. The two parties cooperated in the federal parliament to approve the new region, which was carved out of the Western Region. The other regions were created earlier.

question: One of the major problems of Nigeria federalism is

option.a: imbalance in the structure and sizes of units of federation
option.b: pre-colonial administrative structure among the units of federation
option.c: lack of revenue to cate for the demands of the federation

solution: One major problem of Nigerian federalism is the imbalance in the structure and sizes of the units of the federation. The states differ greatly in size, population and resources, which creates tension over representation and revenue. Inadequate manpower and revenue are problems too, but the structural imbalance is central.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: Which of the following was done during the Gowon administration to reduce regional structural imbalance in the federation?
solution: During the Gowon administration, the government tried to reduce regional structural imbalance through the creation of states. In 1967 the four regions were replaced by twelve states, which weakened the large regions. Revenue allocation and ministerial appointments did not change the structure.

question: One feature of public corporations that was weakened by privatization is
solution: One feature of public corporations that was weakened by privatisation is governmental control. Privatisation transfers ownership and control from government to private investors, so government direction of the enterprise is reduced. Social harmony and immigration are not features of public corporations.

question: A problem of public corporations in Nigeria is
solution: A major problem of public corporations in Nigeria is wastage of resources. They are often poorly managed, overstaffed and inefficient, so money and materials are wasted. Public control and the choice of leadership can contribute, but waste is the clearest problem.

question: One of the main duties of the local government service commission is to

option.a: create an enabling working environment for council workers
option.b: handle requests for the creation of more local governments
option.c: supervise and manage the personnel of local governments

solution: One of the main duties of the Local Government Service Commission is to supervise and manage the personnel of local governments. It recruits, promotes and disciplines local government staff. It does not create local governments or conduct council elections.

question: The option A4 model was used in the conduct of the
solution: The Option A4 model was used in the conduct of the 1993 elections. Voters queued behind their preferred candidates instead of using ballot papers. The system was introduced by the Babangida administration for the 1993 general elections.

question: The review of Nigeria foreign policy under the Murtala-Obasanjo regime was done by
solution: The review of Nigeria's foreign policy under the Murtala-Obasanjo regime was done by the Adedeji Commission. It examined Nigeria's foreign policy interests and recommended a more assertive, Africa-centred approach. The Phillips and Udoji commissions dealt with the civil service.

question: Which of the following is a guiding principle of Nigeria's foreign policy?

option.a: interference in the affairs of African Countries
option.c: total opposition to the cold war
option.d: posting  of only carrier diplomats as envoys

solution: A guiding principle of Nigeria's foreign policy is decolonisation of all African countries. Nigeria supports the independence of African territories and the end of colonial and minority rule. Interfering in other countries' affairs is not a principle.

question: The technical Aids Corps was established during the regime of
solution: The Technical Aid Corps was established during the regime of Ibrahim Babangida in 1987. It sends Nigerian professionals to developing countries, especially in Africa, the Pacific and the Caribbean. Obasanjo, Buhari and Abacha led at other times.

question: The granting of asylum to Charles Taylor by Nigeria was to
solution: The granting of asylum to Charles Taylor by Nigeria was meant to promote peace in Liberia. Nigeria offered him a safe place to live so that the Liberian civil war could end peacefully. It was not done to defy the West or to control Liberia.

question: The main attributes of a state are

option.a: government, the police and the armed forces
option.d: the press, the legislature, the executive and the judiciary

solution: The main attributes of a state are population, territory, government and sovereignty. A state must have people, a defined land area, a government that rules, and independence from outside control. The police, armed forces and press are institutions within the state, not attributes of it.

question: A disadvantage of the one-party system is that it
solution: A disadvantage of the one-party system is that it makes accountability difficult. With no opposition to expose mistakes or challenge the government, leaders are less answerable to the people. The system may actually reduce open political differences rather than emphasise them.

question: In the history of Nigeria, 1914 was the

option.a: year the British established their rule over Nigeria
option.c: year Lugard effected amalgamation of Nigeria
option.d: year the railway system was completed

solution: In Nigerian history, 1914 was the year Lord Lugard effected the amalgamation of Nigeria. He joined the Northern and Southern Protectorates into one colony and protectorate. The First World War also began in 1914, but the question is about Nigeria.

question: How many states were created in Nigeria in 1967?
solution: In 1967, the Gowon government created twelve states in Nigeria. The four regions were broken into smaller states to reduce the power of the regions and bring government closer to the people. Nineteen states came in 1976, and twenty-one in 1987.

question: A major function of Warrant Chiefs was to
solution: A major function of Warrant Chiefs was to take charge of local administration. The British appointed them where there were no recognised traditional rulers, and they collected taxes and kept order. Supervising native courts was only one part of that wider duty.

question: The first Governor-General of Nigeria was
solution: The first Governor-General of Nigeria was Lord Lugard, after the 1914 amalgamation. He governed the whole country as one unit. Nnamdi Azikiwe later became Governor-General and then President, and James Robertson was the last colonial Governor-General.
category: Institutions of Government in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: The main role of pressure groups is to

option.a: influence the legislature to make decision favourable to them
option.d: use all means, including bribery, to achieve their objectives

solution: The main role of pressure groups is to influence the legislature to make decisions favourable to them. They lobby, send memoranda and campaign for laws and policies that benefit their members. Bribery and emotional debate are not their proper role.

question: The OAU was formed in
solution: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) was formed in 1963 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Thirty-two independent African states signed its charter. It was replaced by the African Union in 2002.

question: The first African Secretary-General of the United Nations is
solution: The first African Secretary-General of the United Nations was Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt, who served from 1992 to 1996. Kofi Annan of Ghana came after him. Joe Garba and Ibrahim Gambari were Nigerian diplomats, not Secretaries-General.

question: The system of indirect rule failed in the former Eastern Nigeria primarily because

option.b: the Chief refused to cooperate with colonial officers
option.c: the high incidence of taxation Chief refused to cooperate with colonial officers
option.d: the colonial officers imposed warrant chiefs on the people

solution: Indirect rule failed in the former Eastern Nigeria primarily because of the fragmented political structures. Igbo society had no centralised kings or emirs, so there were no traditional rulers through whom the British could govern. The imposition of warrant chiefs caused resistance and made the system fail.

question: In federalism system of Government currency, Armed forces and National defense is the primary function of
solution: In a federal system, currency, armed forces and national defence are on the exclusive list. That means only the federal government can make laws on them. State and local governments handle other matters, such as local roads and markets.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: In a Federal System (such as Nigeria) the Local Governments are directly responsible

option.a: to the Federal or Central Government
option.c: to the Federal and State Government
option.d: to no other level of government

solution: In a federal system such as Nigeria, local governments are directly responsible to the state government. The state government supervises them, approves their budgets and can create or dissolve them. The federal government deals with them mainly through revenue allocation.

question: Federalism was introduced in Nigeria under the
solution: Federalism was introduced in Nigeria under the Lyttelton Constitution of 1954. It divided powers between the central government and the regions and made the regions stronger. The Richards and Macpherson constitutions came earlier and were less federal.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: Which of these is not the supreme organ of the OAU?

option.c: The Assembly of Heads of States and Government

solution: The item that is not a supreme organ of the OAU is appointment of staff. The supreme organs were the Assembly of Heads of State and Government, the Council of Ministers and the Secretariat. Appointment of staff is an administrative activity, not an organ.

question: When a bill passed by legislature is vetoed by the executive, the action underscores the principle of
solution: When a bill passed by the legislature is vetoed by the executive, the action underscores the principle of checks and balances. Each arm of government can limit the power of the others. Separation of powers explains why the powers are divided, but the veto itself is a check.

question: The Igbo political system was based on
solution: The Igbo political system was based on the Umunna, the extended family or lineage group. Decisions were taken by elders and assemblies of the Umunna rather than by a single king. Age grades and Umuada also played roles, but the Umunna was the foundation.

question: One challenge associated with presidential system of Government
solution: One challenge associated with the presidential system of government is the separation of power. Because the president and the legislature are elected separately, they can belong to different parties and disagree, which may slow down government. Fusion of power belongs to the parliamentary system.

question: The dominant idea behind the establishment of the Organization of African Unity is

option.b: to show the world that Africa can also do what Latin American and Asian countries have done
option.c: to provide a framework and opportunities for co-operation on common African problems
option.d: to promote economic development of Africa

solution: The dominant idea behind the establishment of the OAU was that Africa must unite. African leaders wanted unity, cooperation and freedom from colonial rule. Cooperation on common problems and economic development were parts of that larger goal of unity.

question: Nigeria's quest for a leadership role in Africa hinges principally on her
solution: Nigeria's quest for a leadership role in Africa hinges principally on her economic strength. A strong economy gives Nigeria the resources to support peacekeeping, aid poorer states and lead regional organisations. Size and population matter, but economic strength gives the real capacity to lead.

question: The term, rule of law means

option.b: everybody is equal before the law
option.c: we are being governed by lawyers

solution: The term rule of law means that nobody is above the law and everybody is equal before the law. Both statements are correct, so the answer is A and B above. Being governed by lawyers is a misunderstanding of the term.

question: In the Oyo traditional political system, the Alafin of Oyo was elected or chosen by a group known as
solution: In the Oyo traditional political system, the Alaafin was chosen by a group known as the Oyo Mesi. This council of seven chiefs, led by the Bashorun, also checked the Alaafin's power. The Ogboni were a religious and judicial society, not the body that chose the king.

question: A good example of a country with a largely unwritten constitution is
solution: A good example of a country with a largely unwritten constitution is the United Kingdom. Its constitution is found in statutes, court decisions and conventions rather than in one written document. The United States and Nigeria have written constitutions.

question: The two leaders that played the most prominent roles in the formation of the ECOWAS were
solution: The two leaders who played the most prominent roles in forming ECOWAS were Gowon and Eyadema. Nigeria's General Yakubu Gowon and Togo's President Gnassingbe Eyadema pushed the idea, and the treaty was signed in Lagos in 1975. The other pairs were not the main founders.

question: Under a presidential system of government, the legislature and the executive are

option.a: elected separately to an unfixed term
option.b: appointed at the same time to an unfixed term
option.c: appointed by the judiciary to a fixed term
option.d: elected separately to a fixed term

solution: Under a presidential system, the legislature and the executive are elected separately to a fixed term. The president and legislators each serve a fixed number of years and neither can easily remove the other. This is different from a parliamentary system, where the executive comes from the legislature.

question: Which of these constitutions recognised local government as a third tier of government in Nigeria?
solution: The 1979 Constitution recognised local government as a third tier of government in Nigeria. It gave local governments a share of national revenue and specific functions. The 1960, 1963 and 1946 constitutions did not treat local government as a full third tier.

question: A referendum is a device to ensure that

option.b: legislators vote to resolve contentious issues
option.c: decisions are effected with the consent of citizens
option.d: bye-elections are held to fill vacant positions

solution: A referendum is a device to ensure that decisions are effected with the consent of citizens. The people vote directly on a specific issue, such as a new constitution or a major policy. It is not the same as a general election or a bye-election.

question: The Mid-Western Region was created in Nigeria in
solution: The Mid-Western Region was created in Nigeria in 1963. It was carved out of the Western Region after the NCNC and NPC cooperated in parliament. It later became Bendel State and is now part of Edo and Delta States.

question: One of the principal objectives of the OPEC is to

option.a: determine oil prices in the international market
option.b: harmonise the oil policies of member countries

solution: One of the principal objectives of OPEC is to harmonise the oil policies of member countries. By acting together, members can stabilise prices and protect their income. OPEC influences prices, but its formal aim is to coordinate members' policies.

question: A constitution that requires a plebiscite or a referendum to be amended is
solution: A constitution that requires a plebiscite or referendum to be amended is rigid. The extra step of asking the people makes it hard to change. A flexible constitution can be amended by an ordinary law, and a written constitution is not necessarily rigid.

question: The following are international organisations except
solution: The pressure group is not an international organisation. The OAU, UNO and Commonwealth of Nations are international bodies made up of states. A pressure group is a domestic association that tries to influence government policy.

question: In the Presidential System of Government, the president is elected to office by
solution: In the presidential system, the president is elected to office by the people through direct elections. Voters choose the president separately from the legislature. The cabinet, parliament and military do not elect the president in a democracy.

question: The act of removing an elected official by the electorate is referred to as
solution: The act of removing an elected official by the electorate is called recall. Voters in a constituency can sign a petition to remove their representative before the end of the term. Impeachment is done by the legislature, not the electorate.

question: Which of the following world powers was the first to come to Nigeria's aid during the civil war?
solution: The world power that first came to Nigeria's aid during the civil war was the USSR. The Soviet Union supplied arms and diplomatic support to the federal government when Western countries hesitated. Nigeria's ties with the Soviet Union strengthened as a result.

question: Citizenship refers to the

option.a: legal status of a member of a state
option.d: social status of a person in a state

solution: Citizenship refers to the legal status of a member of a state. A citizen enjoys rights and owes duties under the law. Being an indigenous member or holding a high position is not what defines citizenship.

question: The council constituted by Lord Lugard in 1914 has
solution: The council constituted by Lord Lugard in 1914 had 36 members. It was called the Nigerian Council and included officials and a few traditional rulers. It was largely advisory and met only a few times.

question: Nigeria's withdrawal from the Edinburgh Commonwealth Games in July 1986 was in protest against British

option.b: failure to impose sanctions on South Africa
option.d: support for UNITA rebels in Angola

solution: Nigeria withdrew from the Edinburgh Commonwealth Games in July 1986 to protest against Britain's failure to impose sanctions on South Africa. Nigeria wanted strong action against apartheid, and Britain resisted sanctions. The withdrawal was a statement against apartheid.

question: Which of these rulers resisted colonial rule and was deported to Calabar?
solution: Oba Ovonramwen of Benin resisted British colonial rule and was deported to Calabar in 1897. The British invaded Benin City and removed him from power. King Jaja of Opobo was also deported, but to the West Indies.

question: A state that is ruled by an elected citizen is
solution: A state ruled by an elected citizen is a republic. The head of state is chosen rather than born into the office. A monarchy is hereditary, a plutocracy is rule by the rich, and an empire is a group of territories under one ruler.

question: An electoral process in which candidates are selected for elective offices by party members is
solution: An electoral process in which candidates are selected for elective offices by party members is a primary election. Party members choose their flag-bearer before the general election. An electoral college is a group of electors, and a bye-election fills a single vacant seat.

question: Nigeria spearheaded the formation of ECOWAS during the regime of
solution: Nigeria spearheaded the formation of ECOWAS during the regime of Yakubu Gowon. The treaty was signed in Lagos in 1975. Obasanjo, Murtala Muhammed and Babangida led at other times.

question: A major opposition party at the national level in Nigeria's Second Republic was
solution: A major opposition party at the national level in Nigeria's Second Republic was the Unity Party of Nigeria (UPN). It was led by Chief Obafemi Awolowo and controlled the old Western Region. The NPN was the ruling party, while the PRP and GNPP were smaller parties.
category: Political Parties and Party Politics in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: The exclusion of Africans from colonial administration is associated with
solution: The exclusion of Africans from colonial administration is associated with the policy of assimilation. France aimed to make a few educated Africans French, but it kept real power in French hands and did not admit Africans into senior administration. Indirect rule, by contrast, used African chiefs.

question: During the 1964 Federal Election in Nigeria, the United Progressive Grand Alliance comprised the
solution: In the 1964 Federal Election, the United Progressive Grand Alliance (UPGA) was made up of the UMBC, AG, NEPU and NCNC. It was an alliance of opposition parties against the NPC-led government. The other combinations are not correct.

question: Which of the following binds Commonwealth Nations together?
solution: What binds Commonwealth nations together is their common colonial history. Most members were once part of the British Empire and share legal and administrative traditions. They do not share one political system, currency or language.

question: A structure of government in which power is shared between the centre and the units is
solution: A structure of government in which power is shared between the centre and the units is federalism. Each level has its own powers protected by the constitution. A unitary system concentrates power at the centre, and a confederation gives the units most of the power.

question: Foreign Policy refers to

option.a: a policy made by a country when it is at war
option.b: the general principles of a states international behaviour
option.c: a policy made by a foreign country
option.d: a policy made by a country for foreigners

solution: Foreign policy refers to the general principles of a state's international behaviour. It guides how a country deals with other states on trade, defence, diplomacy and international organisations. It is not a policy made only during war or for foreigners.

question: '' From each according to his ability to each according to his needs' is the principle of
solution: The principle from each according to his ability, to each according to his needs belongs to communism. It describes a classless society where people contribute what they can and receive what they need. Socialism is a step towards it, while capitalism rewards private ownership and profit.

question: The maintenance of law and order is a function of the
solution: The maintenance of law and order is a function of the executive. The police and other security agencies are under the executive arm and enforce the laws. The legislature makes laws, and the judiciary interprets them.

question: The development of attitudes and beliefs about a political system is known as
solution: The development of attitudes and beliefs about a political system is known as political socialisation. Family, school, religion, peers and the media transmit these attitudes over time. Political orientation is the result, not the process.

question: A nation could be identified through its
solution: A nation can be identified through its common language and culture. A nation is a group of people who share a sense of identity, history and culture. Population size, military strength or a constitution may belong to a state, but they do not create a nation.

question: A network of groups of people in an institution expressing human association is
solution: A network of groups of people in an institution expressing human association is a society. People live together in organised relationships with shared norms and institutions. A community is smaller, while a nation and a state are political ideas.

question: The Commission on Mediation, Conciliation and Arbitration is an organ of
solution: The Commission on Mediation, Conciliation and Arbitration is an organ of the African Union. It helps to settle disputes between member states peacefully. It is not an organ of the UN, Commonwealth or OPEC.

question: The policy of assimilation was the colonial policy of the
solution: The policy of assimilation was the colonial policy of the French. France tried to turn educated Africans into French citizens by teaching French language, culture and law. Britain used indirect rule, while Portugal and Germany used other methods.

question: The appointment, promotion and discipline of civil servants is the responsibility of the
solution: The appointment, promotion and discipline of civil servants is the responsibility of the Civil Service Commission. It handles personnel matters to keep the service professional and neutral. The Public Complaints Commission handles citizens' complaints, and the Judicial Service Commission handles judges.

question: A country is said to operate an unwritten constitution if the

option.a: constitution is not contained in a single document
option.c: existing constitution can be suspended at will
option.d: country is not having a printed constitution

solution: A country operates an unwritten constitution if the constitution is not contained in a single document. It is found in statutes, court decisions and conventions, as in Britain. It does not mean the rules are never written down or that the constitution can be suspended at will.

question: The form of government headed by a king is
solution: The form of government headed by a king is a monarchy. The king may be an absolute ruler or a constitutional monarch with limited powers. Presidentialism and republicanism have elected heads, and fascism is a dictatorial ideology.

question: Citizens exercise their sovereignty by

option.d: their right to sue the state

solution: Citizens exercise their sovereignty by voting at elections. Through the ballot they choose their leaders and decide who will govern them. Attending rallies or registering to vote are preparations, but the actual exercise of sovereignty is voting.

question: Which of these is an attribute of government?
solution: An attribute of government is political power. Government is the institution that makes and enforces decisions for the state, and it does so through political power. Sovereignty, a constitution and a definite territory are attributes of the state, not of government.

question: Nigerian Judiciary is headed by
solution: The Nigerian judiciary is headed by the Chief Justice of the Federation. He or she presides over the Supreme Court, the highest court in the land. The Attorney-General is the chief law officer of the executive, not the head of the judiciary.

question: The modern theory of sovereignty was popularized by
solution: The modern theory of sovereignty was popularised by Jean Bodin. In the sixteenth century he described sovereignty as the supreme and absolute power of the state. Hobbes, Locke and Montesquieu wrote about government, but Bodin is the key theorist of sovereignty.

question: Public opinion is commonly referred to as the composite reaction of the citizenry on
solution: Public opinion is commonly referred to as the composite reaction of the citizenry on key issues that affect them. It is what people think and say about matters that concern their lives and the nation. It is wider than matters affecting government alone.

question: In order to assist fellow developing countries, Nigeria initiated the

option.b: Economic Community of West African States

solution: To assist fellow developing countries, Nigeria initiated the Technical Aid Corps Scheme. It sends Nigerian doctors, teachers, engineers and other professionals to needy countries, mainly in Africa, the Pacific and the Caribbean. NEPAD and ECOWAS are regional bodies, not Nigerian aid schemes.

question: In the Igbo traditional system, the highest democratic institution is the
solution: In the Igbo traditional system, the highest democratic institution was the Oha-na-eze. This assembly of elders and representatives discussed and decided important matters for the community. The Umunna was the extended family, and the Umuada was the daughters' group.

question: Separation of powers as an ingredient of the presidential system implies the

option.c: distinction between head of state and head of government

solution: Separation of powers in the presidential system implies the sharing of governmental powers. The constitution divides power among the legislature, executive and judiciary so that each can check the others. It is not about levels of government or the head of state.

question: The major objective of pressure group is to
solution: The major objective of a pressure group is to influence government. It tries to shape laws, policies and appointments in favour of its members. It does not seek to form or change the government, which is the aim of a political party.

question: In Nigeria, the foundations of federalism was laid by the
solution: In Nigeria, the foundations of federalism were laid by the Richards Constitution of 1946. It divided the country into three regions with their own legislatures, starting the move towards federalism. The Lyttelton Constitution later strengthened the federal structure.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: Franchise can be described as the right to
solution: Franchise is the right to vote and be voted for. It covers both choosing leaders and being chosen as a candidate. The right to form parties or contest elections alone does not fully describe franchise.

question: A major factor that necessitated the adoption of federalism in Nigeria was the
solution: A major factor that led Nigeria to adopt federalism was the diversity of culture and language. Many different ethnic groups needed a system that allowed them to govern their own affairs while sharing a central government. Creating states and natural resources came later or were not the main reason.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: The office of the Prime Minister in Nigeria was created in
solution: The office of Prime Minister in Nigeria was created in 1957. Abubakar Tafawa Balewa became the first Prime Minister as Nigeria moved towards independence. The office did not exist in 1951 or 1954, and 1959 was the year of the federal election.
category: Institutions of Government in Post-Independence Nigeria

question: The Nigeria Police is an agency of the
solution: The Nigeria Police is an agency of the executive arm of government. It enforces laws and maintains order under the control of the executive. It is not part of the judiciary, the Ministry of Defence or the Ministry of Interior.

question: The legislature checks the excesses of the executive through
solution: The legislature checks the excesses of the executive through scrutiny of the budget. It examines and approves government spending, and it can refuse or amend proposals. Appointing civil servants and nominating judges are executive or shared functions.

question: Government by the best citizens is referred to as
solution: Government by the best citizens is referred to as aristocracy. In Aristotle's classification, it is rule by a few good people for the common good. Democracy is rule by the people, oligarchy is rule by a few for themselves, and plutocracy is rule by the rich.

question: The charter establishing the AU was signed in
solution: The charter establishing the African Union was signed in Togo. The Constitutive Act of the African Union was adopted in Lome, Togo, in 2000, and the AU was launched in Durban in 2002. Libya hosted the Sirte Declaration, and Ethiopia hosted the OAU.

question: In Nigeria, items in the exclusive list are under the jurisdiction of
solution: In Nigeria, items on the exclusive list are under the jurisdiction of the central government. Only the federal government can legislate on them, and they include defence, currency and foreign affairs. State and local governments handle other matters.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: Which of these factors motivated colonialism in Africa?
solution: The factor that motivated colonialism in Africa was economic interest. European powers wanted raw materials, markets and investment opportunities. Scientific and cultural superiority and humanitarianism were used as excuses, but economic gain was the real motive.

question: The responsibility of giving policy guidelines to the board of corporations rest with the
solution: The responsibility of giving policy guidelines to the board of a corporation rests with the Minister. The minister represents the government and sets the broad direction, while the board manages the corporation. The chairman and permanent secretary do not give government policy guidelines.

question: Which of these institutions make bye-laws?
solution: Local Government Councils make bye-laws. These are local laws that deal with matters such as markets, sanitation and local roads. The National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly make laws for their own levels, and the Council of State advises the president.

question: Federal and State governments legislate on items in the
solution: Federal and State governments legislate on items in the concurrent list. Both levels can make laws on these matters, but federal law prevails if there is a conflict. The exclusive list belongs to the federal government alone, and the residual list belongs to the states.

question: In Nigeria, public corporations are established by
solution: In Nigeria, public corporations are established by an act of parliament. The law sets out the corporation's powers, functions and management. Executive orders, bye-laws and military decrees are not the normal way of creating them today.

question: In the Hausa pre-colonial political system, the spiritual and political powers were vested in the
solution: In the Hausa pre-colonial political system, spiritual and political powers were vested in the Emir. He was both the political ruler and the religious leader of the emirate. The Madawaki, Galadima and Waziri were senior officials under him.

question: The Constitutional forms with two levels of Government is _________
solution: A confederation is a constitutional arrangement with two levels of government: a weak central government and strong component states. The states keep most powers and only give limited powers to the centre. A unitary system has one level, while a federation shares power more evenly.

question: The essence of ECOWAS is to________

option.b: foster interstate economic and political co-operation

solution: The essence of ECOWAS is to foster interstate economic and political cooperation among West African states. It promotes trade, free movement of people and joint development. It is not a body for bringing political parties together.

question: The head of government under the 1979 Constitution is the _____

option.c: speaker of the house of represenative

solution: The head of government under the 1979 Constitution was the president. The constitution created an executive president who was both head of state and head of government. The office of prime minister belonged to the parliamentary system before 1966.

question: The characteristics of the Civil Servants which prevent its officers from addressing the press unless directed is known as ________
solution: The civil service rule that prevents officers from addressing the press unless directed is called anonymity. Civil servants work quietly behind ministers and do not speak publicly for the government. Impartiality and neutrality refer to political fairness, not to speaking to the press.

question: The granting of internal authority to the regions came under which constitution?
solution: The granting of internal authority to the regions came under the Richards Constitution of 1946. It created regional councils with some powers over local matters, which was the beginning of federalism. The Lyttelton Constitution later increased regional powers.

question: In the year 1911, who argued most representative system deteriorates towards an Oligarchy or Patriarchy?
solution: In 1911, Robert Michels argued that even the most representative system tends to become an oligarchy. This is his famous iron law of oligarchy: organisations become controlled by a small group of leaders. The other names are not associated with this idea.

question: In the 18th century, a new wind of development blew over Europe and the development was referred to__________?
solution: In the eighteenth century, a new wind of development blew over Europe and it was called the Industrial Revolution. Machines, factories and new methods of production changed economies and societies. It was not a labour, doctrine or purely economic revolution in name.

question: One major merit of the Unitary system of government is that_______?
solution: One major merit of the unitary system is that it is cheaper to operate. There is only one central government and one set of institutions, so less money is spent on duplicated offices. It is not necessarily more democratic, and it can encourage rather than end tyranny.

question: The legal right to exercise power in a state is known as______
solution: The legal right to exercise power in a state is known as authority. Authority is power that is recognised as legitimate by those who are governed. Sovereignty is the supreme power of the state, coercion is forced compliance, and influence is the ability to affect decisions without formal power.

question: Bills passed by the legislature usually requires the approval of the following except_______
solution: Bills passed by the legislature usually require the approval of the President, Governor or Monarch, depending on the system. A member of the House of Representatives does not approve a bill after it has been passed. The member only takes part in the debate and voting.

question: Dispute among member state of ECOWAS are settled by _________?
solution: Disputes among ECOWAS member states are settled by the Community Tribunal. It interprets the ECOWAS treaty and decides cases brought before it. The Technical and Specialised Commission and the Council of Ministers handle other matters.

question: ___ is the act of wearing campaign paraphernalia or carrying signs to a polling centre with the intent of influencing voters?
solution: Wearing campaign paraphernalia or carrying signs to a polling centre to influence voters is called passive electioneering. It is a form of campaigning too close to the polling area and is usually restricted by electoral law. A polling centre is the place of voting, not the act.

question: The totality of Nigeria's participation in the international system is known as ______?
solution: The totality of Nigeria's participation in the international system is known as foreign policy. It covers diplomacy, trade, defence and membership of international organisations. Economic and social policies are domestic policies.

question: one important agent of a political socialization is the _______?
solution: One important agent of political socialisation is the political party. Parties teach members about politics, mobilise them and spread ideas through campaigns. A party constitution is a document, and an electoral college is a voting body, not an agent of socialisation.

question: The primary source of fund for local government is ________?
solution: The primary source of funds for local government is statutory allocation. Local governments receive a share of the federation account as required by law. Grants and loans are additional sources, and fines are only a small part of local revenue.

question: The United Nations is a replacement for which ineffective organisation?
solution: The United Nations is a replacement for the League of Nations. The League failed to prevent the Second World War, so the UN was formed in 1945 to maintain peace and security. OPEC and ECOWAS are regional or economic bodies.

question: Which of the following emphasizes the rule of law and human rights protection?
solution: Constitutionalism emphasises the rule of law and the protection of human rights. It means that government must act within the limits of the constitution and respect citizens' rights. Delegated legislation, decentralisation and centralisation are different ideas.

question: Laws enacted by the legislature are known as ___ ?
solution: Laws enacted by the legislature are known as legislation. The legislature is the body that makes them, and a budget is a financial plan. The executive implements laws, and the judiciary interprets them.

question: The Quorum in the OPEC conference is formed with the attendance of ?

option.a: one third of the member state
option.d: three quarter of the member state

solution: The quorum at the OPEC conference is formed by three quarters of the member states. This ensures that major decisions are taken only when most members are present. A simple majority or half of the members is not enough.

question: Bye laws are made by the _______?
solution: Bye-laws are made by the executive or by bodies to which the legislature has delegated power, such as local councils. They deal with local or administrative matters. The legislature makes the main laws, and the judiciary interprets them.

question: The organ of the UN that served as custodial of some African countries prior to their independence is _________?
solution: The UN organ that served as custodian of some African countries before their independence was the Trusteeship Council. It supervised trust territories and guided them towards self-government. The General Assembly and Security Council had different roles.

question: The chairman of the 1976 constitution drafting committee was _____?
solution: The chairman of the 1976 Constitution Drafting Committee was Chief Rotimi Williams. The committee prepared the draft that became the 1979 Constitution. Udo Udoma, Ademola Adetokunbo and Niki Tobi served in other legal roles.

question: The needs of the citizen are made known to the government through ____?
solution: The needs of citizens are made known to government through public opinion. Through the media, petitions, protests and surveys, people express what they want and how they feel. The judiciary, parties and civil service also play roles, but public opinion is the direct channel.

question: The organ that is responsible for the interpretation of law is known as _____?
solution: The organ responsible for interpreting the law is the judiciary. Courts explain what the law means and apply it to cases. The legislature makes laws, and the executive implements them.

question: New partnership for Africa's development was an attempt to overcome _______?
solution: The New Partnership for Africa's Development (NEPAD) was an attempt to overcome obstacles to African development. It aimed to promote good governance, investment and growth across the continent. Civil wars, disease and coups are some of those obstacles, but the broad aim was development.

question: The problem that has bedeviled many developing societies is known as ______?
solution: The problem that has bedevilled many developing societies is corruption. It diverts public resources, weakens institutions and discourages investment. Enforcement, impartiality and weak courts are related issues, but corruption is the central problem.

question: A formal group decision-making process by which a population chooses an individual to hold public office is ___ ?
solution: A formal group decision-making process by which a population chooses an individual to hold public office is an election. Through elections, voters choose their representatives and leaders. A by-election fills one vacant seat, and a bill is a proposed law.

question: The system of government by the political parties in a democratic country is known as ______?
solution: The system of government by political parties in a democratic country is known as the party system. It describes whether a country has one, two or many parties. A political party is a single organisation, and public opinion is what people think.

question: Ensuring that appointment into federal establishment in Nigeria reflect geographical spread is the sole function of the ____?

option.a: revenue Mobilization and fiscal allocation commission

solution: Ensuring that appointments into federal establishments reflect geographical spread is the function of the Federal Character Commission. It monitors recruitment and appointments so that all states and regions are represented. The revenue commission, civil service commission and public complaints commission have other duties.

question: The transfer of certain powers and functions by means of constitutional or legislation process to the lowest levels of government is known as ___ ?
solution: The transfer of certain powers and functions, by constitutional or legislative process, to the lowest levels of government is known as devolution. Power is passed down permanently to local authorities. Delegation is temporary, deconcentration is administrative, and decentralisation is the wider term.

question: When was the Nigeria flag designed?
solution: The Nigerian flag was designed in 1959. Taiwo Akinkunmi, a student, won the national competition for the design. Nigeria became independent the following year, 1960.

question: The elective principle was introduced by which constitution?
solution: The elective principle was introduced by the Clifford Constitution of 1922. It allowed a few Nigerians to be elected to the Legislative Council, the first time elections were held. The Richards, Macpherson and Lyttelton constitutions came later.

question: The primary reason for the establishment of political parties is to _______?
solution: The primary reason for establishing political parties is to attain political power. Parties contest elections so that they can form government and carry out their programmes. Protecting interests and lobbying are the work of pressure groups.

question: The African country that was not colonised is ______?
solution: The African country that was not colonised is Ethiopia. It defeated Italy at Adwa in 1896 and kept its independence, apart from a short Italian occupation in the 1930s. Sudan, Botswana and Gambia were colonised.

question: A major differences between pressure group and political party is that whereas the latter aims at winning power the former__________?
solution: The major difference between a pressure group and a political party is that, whereas the party aims at winning power, the pressure group aims at influencing government policies. It does not contest elections to form government. It works to shape decisions in favour of its members.

question: Which of the following is a process of military disengagement from Nigerian politics?

option.b: conduct of free and fair elections
option.c: Appointment of Army officers into political post

solution: A process of military disengagement from Nigerian politics is the conduct of free and fair elections. Elections allow civilians to take over power and return the soldiers to the barracks. Increasing the military budget or appointing officers to political posts keeps the military involved.

question: Division of responsibilities into distinct branches to limit any branches from exercising the core functions of another is _______?
solution: The division of responsibilities into distinct branches, to stop one branch from exercising the core functions of another, is separation of powers. Each arm has its own duties and can check the others. Fusion of power is the opposite.

question: In the 1976 reforms and the local government generally, which regime constitutes the Ibrahim panel of 1984?
solution: The Ibrahim Panel of 1984 was constituted under the Major General Muhammadu Buhari Administration. It reviewed local government reforms and administration. Obasanjo, Jonathan and Shonekan led at other times.

question: Iran, Iraq and which countries first created OPEC?
solution: OPEC was first created by Iran, Iraq, Venezuela, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait. These five countries founded the organisation in Baghdad in 1960. Dubai, Greece and Vienna were not founding members.

question: One of the demerits of the privatisation of public corporations in Nigeria is?

option.b: higher cost of goods and services

solution: One demerit of privatising public corporations in Nigeria is the higher cost of goods and services. Private owners may raise prices to make profit, and the poor may suffer. Privatisation is usually intended to improve efficiency, not to create scarcity or unemployment.

question: The second ballot is based on the principle that a successful candidate must obtain
solution: The second ballot is used when no candidate wins outright in the first round. It is based on the principle that a successful candidate must obtain an absolute majority, that is, more than half of all the valid votes cast. A simple majority only means having more votes than any other candidate.

question: The tenure of the president of the UN Security Council is
solution: The President of the United Nations Security Council serves for one month. The fifteen members of the Council take turns to hold the presidency, rotating in alphabetical order of their country names. This keeps the leadership of the Council shared and short.

question: Political authority is vested in the_________
solution: Political authority is vested in the state. Authority is power that is accepted as legitimate, and the state is the body that gives laws their binding force. The government, judiciary and armed forces only exercise authority on behalf of the state.

question: Unicameral legislatures are popular in
solution: Unicameral legislatures are popular in a unitary system of government. In a unitary state there is one central legislature, so a single chamber is enough. Federal states usually need a second chamber to represent their component units.

question: In the cabinet system of government, individual responsibility of ministers means that ____________

option.a: only ministers can be held responsible for errors
option.b: a minister must hold his subordinates responsible for his failures
option.c: the prime ministers can remove an erring minister
option.d: no individual can be held responsible for government decisions

solution: In the cabinet system, individual responsibility of ministers means that only ministers can be held responsible for errors in their own ministries. Each minister answers personally for the work of the department he or she heads, and must resign if seriously at fault.

question: An important aspect of an unwritten constitution is that it

option.a: is easy to understand to everybody

solution: An important aspect of an unwritten constitution is that it contains customary laws and conventions. The rules are found in traditions, court decisions and accepted practices rather than in one single document. This is why it is also called a conventional constitution.

question: In 1993, Nigerian troops were on peace-keeping assignment to
solution: In 1993, Nigerian troops were on peace-keeping assignment in Liberia and Somalia. Nigeria led the ECOMOG force in Liberia and also sent troops to the United Nations operation in Somalia. Burundi, Rwanda and Chad were not the main assignments of that year.

question: Power refers to the__________

option.a: ability to impose one’s will upon others
option.b: duties an individual imposes on himself
option.d: duties political parties demand of their registered members

solution: Power is the ability to impose one's will upon others, even when they resist. It may come from wealth, position, force or influence. Duties people impose on themselves or the legal nature of a constitution are not what power means.

question: The creation of more states in Nigeria has_______

option.b: reduced the gap between the rich and poor states
option.c: increased the powers of the federal government
option.d: increased the powers of the states and local government

solution: The creation of more states in Nigeria was intended to eliminate ethnic and religious conflicts by bringing government closer to the people and giving smaller groups their own states. This is the reason usually given for the policy, even though tensions have not fully disappeared.

question: An Agency of the united Nations which specializes in the welfare of children is the _______
solution: UNICEF is the United Nations agency that specialises in the welfare of children. It provides health care, nutrition, education and protection for children in need. WHO deals with health generally, UNESCO with education and culture, and UNDP with development.

question: A society that is politically organized under a government is called
solution: A society that is politically organised under a government is called a polity. The term describes the organised political community and its system of rule. A community is smaller, and a state adds the idea of sovereignty.

question: In the Oyo empire, the Alaafin was
solution: In the Oyo Empire, the Alaafin was a constitutional monarch. He did not rule alone: the Oyomesi, led by the Bashorun, could check his power, and the Ogboni also advised him. That is why he is described as a limited rather than absolute ruler.

question: Nigeria broke diplomatic relations with France in 1961 because of_________

option.a: her poor relations with the Francophone countries
option.b: France atomic test in the sahara desert
option.d: General de-Gaulle’s negative attitude towards her

solution: Nigeria broke diplomatic relations with France in 1961 because of France's atomic test in the Sahara Desert. Nigeria protested that the test exposed Africans to radiation and showed contempt for the continent. It was not caused by France's ties with Israel or de Gaulle's attitude.

question: In 1991, the African Economic Community Treaty was signed in
solution: The African Economic Community Treaty was signed in Abuja in 1991. It aimed to create a common African market and economic union. Addis Ababa, Lome and Tripoli hosted other African agreements.

question: Based on its objectives, the Organization of African Unity can primarily be classified as
solution: Based on its objectives, the Organisation of African Unity can primarily be classified as a political organisation. Its main aims were African unity, decolonisation and cooperation between independent African states. It was not mainly social, cultural or economic.

question: A major feature of the system of government in the Sokoto Caliphate was that

option.a: it was based on customs and traditions

solution: A major feature of the government of the Sokoto Caliphate was that it was theocratic. The Sultan ruled in the name of Islam, and Islamic law guided the administration. It was not a democracy, and power was centralised rather than decentralised.

question: The goal of the theory of separation of power is to

option.a: make the executive dependent on the legislative
option.b: give more powers to the legislative

solution: The goal of the theory of separation of powers is to protect individual liberty. When law-making, execution and adjudication are in different hands, no single arm can become too powerful and oppress the people. Efficiency of the judiciary is not the main aim.

question: The major difference between a state and a nation is that the latter presupposes a _______
solution: The major difference between a state and a nation is that a nation presupposes a homogeneous population. A nation is a people who share a common identity, culture and history, while a state is a political and legal unit. A state can contain many nations.

question: The primary function of the judiciary is to ______
solution: The primary function of the judiciary is to interpret laws. Courts explain what the law means and apply it to disputes between people or between people and the state. Making laws belongs to the legislature, and executing them belongs to the executive.

question: A constitution of any country is basically___________

option.b: a guide to how the country should be governed
option.c: a document stating what the leaders should do
option.d: a document stating how to acquire power

solution: A constitution is basically a guide to how the country should be governed. It sets out the organs of government, their powers and the rights and duties of citizens. It is not merely a piece of paper or a document only for leaders.

question: The highest decision-making body in Nigeria under the Buhari's military regime was the ________
solution: The highest decision-making body in Nigeria under Buhari's military regime was the Supreme Military Council. It made laws and took major policy decisions after the 1983 coup. The Armed Forces Ruling Council came later under Babangida.

question: A system of government in which the central government is supreme over other levels is
solution: A system of government in which the central government is supreme over other levels is a unitary system. The centre may create, change or abolish local authorities and can overrule them. In a federation, power is shared and protected by the constitution.

question: The main source of local government finance since the 1976 reform has been___________

option.c: revenue from court fines and licences

solution: The main source of local government finance since the 1976 reform has been the federal government. Local governments receive a statutory share of the federation account, which is far larger than rates, levies or court fines.

question: Nigeria is a member of____________
