option.d: The Commonwealth of Nations, OPEC and the OAS

solution: Nigeria is a member of the OAU, the UNO and ECOWAS. These are the Organisation of African Unity (now African Union), the United Nations and the Economic Community of West African States. Nigeria does not belong to NATO or the OAS.

question: A bye-law is made by
solution: A bye-law is made by the local government. It deals with local matters such as markets, sanitation, streets and local levies. Parliament and congress make national laws, and an electoral college only chooses candidates.

question: A human community that is usually cohesive and homogeneous is a
solution: A human community that is usually cohesive and homogeneous is a nation. Its people share a common identity, culture, language or history. A state is a political and legal unit, and a clan is only a family group.

question: Political socialisation is associated with
solution: Political socialisation is associated with the transmission of political values. Family, school, religion, peers and the media pass on beliefs and attitudes about politics from one generation to the next. Military takeovers and transitions are events, not socialisation.

question: OPEC has strong influence with the__________
solution: OPEC has strong influence with the AU. Many African countries are oil producers or importers, so OPEC's decisions on output and prices affect Africa, and it works with the African Union on these matters. It does not control the IMF, EU or ADB.

question: Rhodesia was the former name of
solution: Rhodesia was the former name of Zimbabwe. The white minority government declared independence in 1965, and the country became Zimbabwe in 1980 after majority rule. Zambia was Northern Rhodesia, and Namibia was South West Africa.

question: Citizenship of a state by descent requires that______

option.a: one is born and bred in the state
option.b: one’s mother was born in the state
option.c: one’s grand parents were citizens of that state
option.d: one is domiciled in that state

solution: Citizenship by descent requires that one's grandparents were citizens of that state. A person can claim citizenship through the blood line of parents or grandparents, even if born elsewhere. Being born in the country describes citizenship by birth, not descent.

question: The institutions which constitute the main organs of the government of a nation are the___________

option.c: legislature, the executive and the judiciary

solution: The main organs of government are the legislature, the executive and the judiciary. The legislature makes laws, the executive implements them, and the judiciary interprets them. The civil service and senate are parts of these organs, not the whole structure.

question: One major achievement of the Clifford constitution was_________

option.a: creating a Northern majority in the legislative council
option.c: amalgamating the Northern and Southern provinces

solution: One major achievement of the Clifford Constitution of 1922 was establishing the legislative council for the whole colony and protectorate. It also introduced the elective principle. It did not create a Northern majority or introduce indirect rule.

question: The British government revoked the charter of the Royal Niger Company and took over the administration of Nigeria in which year?
solution: The British government revoked the charter of the Royal Niger Company and took over the administration of Nigeria in 1900. The company had governed the area since 1886, and Britain then ruled directly through its own officials. Amalgamation came later, in 1914.

question: The fundamental rights of citizens include rights to___________

option.a: free education, employment and freedom of thought

solution: The fundamental rights of citizens include the rights to life, speech and association. These are the basic freedoms that allow a person to live, express views and join with others. Free education and social security are desirable but are not fundamental rights in the strict sense.

question: A major feature of the pre-colonial Igbo political system was that___________

option.b: it was based on customs and traditions

solution: A major feature of the pre-colonial Igbo political system was that power was effectively decentralised. Villages, councils of elders, age grades and title societies shared authority, and there was no king ruling everyone. It was neither autocratic nor theocratic.

question: Which of the following spearheaded the transformation of the Organization of African Unity into the African Union?
solution: Thabo Mbeki of South Africa spearheaded the transformation of the Organisation of African Unity into the African Union. He pushed the new vision of a stronger continental body, which was launched in 2002. Nkrumah and Macaulay belonged to an earlier era.

question: All of the following are examples of public corporation in Nigeria EXCEPT?
solution: Zenith Bank plc is not a public corporation. It is a private commercial bank owned by shareholders. JAMB, the Nigerian Steel Development Authority and the Nigeria Railway Corporation are all government-owned public bodies.

question: The role of an Alkali under the Hausa-Fulani political system is primarily to _____________
solution: Under the Hausa-Fulani political system, the role of an Alkali was primarily to adjudicate under Islamic laws. He was a judge who heard cases and applied Islamic law in the emirate. Making laws belonged to the emir, and executing them was the work of other officials.

question: Capitalism is an economic system which emphasizes_______________
solution: Capitalism is an economic system which emphasises individualism. Private individuals own the means of production and are free to run businesses for profit. Communism and collectivism call for common ownership, and internationalism is about cooperation between nations.

question: A government controlled by a few people for their own interests is said to be____________
solution: A government controlled by a few people for their own interests is an oligarchy. The few rule selfishly rather than for the common good. Autocracy is rule by one person, tyranny is cruel rule, and monarchy is rule by a king or queen.

question: In a democratic system _______
solution: In a democratic system, legal sovereignty should not be unquestionable. The law and the constitution can be changed by the people through their representatives, and no authority is above criticism. A democracy allows debate, dissent and peaceful change, so no law is treated as permanently beyond question.

question: That type of sovereignty that thrives on legitimacy is__________

option.b: vested on any form of government

solution: The type of sovereignty that thrives on legitimacy is the one within the people's mandate. A government has this sovereignty when the people accept it as rightful and have chosen it. External and legal sovereignty are about outside recognition and law, not about the people's consent.

question: The right of a citizen to seek redress means the right to________

option.c: seek an appeal under another judgement

solution: The right of a citizen to seek redress means the right to seek an appeal under another judgement. A person who is not satisfied with a court's decision may take the case to a higher court. Fair hearing is part of the trial itself, not the appeal that follows it.

question: An order compelling a lower court or public corporation to perform in accordance with legitimacy is called_________
solution: An order compelling a lower court or public body to perform its lawful duty is the writ of mandamus. It is issued by a higher court to force an official or body to do what the law requires. It is not called the great writ or the writ of the ombudsman.

question: A form of government which has its slogan to be 'ruling of the best' is__________
solution: A form of government whose slogan is rule of the best is aristocracy. The word comes from Greek and means rule by the best or most gifted citizens. Democracy is rule by the people, timocracy is rule by property owners, and plutocracy is rule by the rich.

question: Deconcentration of power means the_______

option.a: sharing of powers among tiers of government
option.b: creation of semi autonomous units to govern other parts of a state
option.c: process of setting strategies or policies for the subsidiary territories in the state by putting recognized personnel in place
option.d: act of delegating powers and authority to component units that exist in a state

solution: Deconcentration of power means setting strategies or policies for subsidiary territories by putting recognised personnel in place. The centre sends its own officials to manage outlying areas, but the officials remain under central control. It is not the same as sharing power among tiers of government.

question: The concept of the independence of the judiciary means that________

option.a: The judiciary must not attempt to meddle into legislative and executive affairs
option.b: The powers of the courts can not be subjected of executive re-assessment
option.c: The sanctity of the office of the Judges and Justices must be preserved without prejudice
option.d: All means of legislative or executive influence on judicial decision making must be disabled

solution: The independence of the judiciary means that all means of legislative or executive influence on judicial decision-making must be disabled. Judges must decide cases freely, without pressure, threats or instructions from politicians. Preserving the dignity of judges is important, but the core idea is freedom from interference.

question: The political party serves as________

option.a: A platform upon which the rights and liberties of the people can be attained
option.b: The group aggregating the interest of all in the state
option.c: A platform for rebelling against military rule

solution: A political party serves as a platform for interest representation. It brings together the demands of different groups and presents them in elections and in government. Rebelling against military rule is not its normal purpose.

question: A party can be said to have national outlook if________

option.a: it is ethnic based but has branches all over the state
option.b: its membership cut across ethnic boundaries
option.c: it is registered by the electoral commission as a national party
option.d: it is headed by individuals who are famous within and without the country

solution: A party can be said to have a national outlook if its membership cuts across ethnic boundaries. Such a party draws members from many ethnic groups and regions, so it represents the whole country rather than one section. Registration alone does not make a party truly national.

question: Argumentation, negotiation and deliberation on the subject matter of a bill begins at the_______
solution: Argumentation, negotiation and deliberation on a bill begin at the second reading. At this stage members debate the general principles of the bill before it goes to the committee stage. The first reading is only the formal introduction of the bill.

question: A vote of no confidence means______

option.a: the same as impeachment in a presidential system
option.b: the ability of the head of state to dissolve the parliament when collective responsibility fails to hold
option.c: the act of showing disapproval to the prime minister having breached the collective responsibility doctrine
option.d: the disapproval with dismissal in effect, the ministers and its head

solution: A vote of no confidence means disapproval with dismissal in effect of the ministers and their head. When parliament passes it, the prime minister and cabinet must resign or call an election. It is not the same as impeachment in a presidential system.

question: A cabinet reshuffle takes place......

option.a: only when a motion of no confidence is passed
option.c: when prorogation and collective responsibility have their way
option.d: when the shadow cabinet fails in its effectiveness

solution: A cabinet reshuffle takes place when dissolution is held. After parliament is dissolved and a new government is formed, the prime minister reorganises the cabinet by moving or replacing ministers. A motion of no confidence may lead to resignation, not automatically to a reshuffle.

question: Popular political participation means________

option.a: having majority of the people partaking in politics
option.b: having a good number of voters in the electoral process
option.c: the aggregate efforts of more than half of the citizens to partake in public debate and politics
option.d: the sum total of all activities exerted by the majority with enthusiasm actively involving in all aspects of their political sphere

solution: Popular political participation means the sum total of all activities exerted by the majority with enthusiasm, actively involving themselves in all aspects of their political sphere. It is not just voting; it includes joining parties, attending meetings, debating and contesting. A good number of voters alone is too narrow.

question: The area from which one or more members or representatives are elected in public offices is called the electoral ........
solution: The area from which one or more representatives are elected is the electoral constituency. Each constituency returns a member to the legislature. A ward is a smaller unit, and an electoral college is a body of electors, not an area.

question: Citizenship by naturalization________

option.a: is the same as citizenship by marriage and registeration
option.b: refers to the process of attaining citizenship through honorary means
option.c: is the act of a non-citizen having satisfied the constitutional criteria becoming a legal member of a state
option.d: is the medium by which an alien through the judiciary receives certification and attains citizenship by birth

solution: Citizenship by naturalisation is the act of a non-citizen who has satisfied the constitutional criteria becoming a legal member of a state. The person applies, meets the residence and character requirements, and takes the oath of allegiance. It is not the same as citizenship by marriage or by birth.

question: The last measure used by the pressure groups issuing a condition to be satisfied within a stipulated time is called_______
solution: The last measure used by a pressure group when it issues a condition to be met within a fixed time is an ultimatum. It warns the government that action will follow if the demand is not met. Lobbying and dialogue are peaceful and earlier steps, while a strike is the action that may follow.

question: Generally, a political party with only manifestoes without fulfilment is a/an _____
solution: A political party with only manifestoes and no fulfilment is an elitist party. It is controlled by a small group of leaders who make promises to win votes but do not carry them out for the people. A conservative party wants to preserve tradition, which is a different idea.

question: A form of government organized by a council of military officers is called______
solution: A form of government organised by a council of military officers is a military junta. A group of officers takes power and rules together, usually after a coup. Stratocracy is rule by the army as a whole, and mobocracy is rule by a mob.

question: The non-stratified society in the pre-colonial era was that of the ........ where decisions were made________
solution: The non-stratified society in the pre-colonial era was that of the Igbo, where decisions were made by consensus. Igbo society had no kings or ranked classes; elders and assemblies discussed issues until they agreed. The Yoruba and Hausa-Fulani had clear rulers and ranks.

question: The Hausa/Fulani Empire as a result of its heterogeneous population adopted_________

option.a: A unitary system where full concentration of power prevailed
option.b: A federal structure where powers were decentralized although autocratic
option.c: A quasi federal structure with devolution
option.d: A partial federal set up with deconcentration

solution: The Hausa/Fulani Empire, because of its heterogeneous population, adopted a partial federal set-up with deconcentration. The emirs ruled their emirates under the Sultan, but the centre sent officials and kept overall control. It was not a full federation and not a pure unitary system.

question: Twelve States creation is a known achievement of the ... regime
solution: The creation of twelve states is a known achievement of the Yakubu Gowon regime. In 1967 Gowon replaced the four regions with twelve states. Murtala Muhammed created nineteen states in 1976, and Babangida created more later.

question: The basis of the Nigerian foreign policy thrust particularly during the Independence Constitution era was ... in nature
solution: The basis of Nigeria's foreign policy during the Independence Constitution era was afrocentric in nature. Nigeria put Africa at the centre of its foreign relations, supporting decolonisation and African unity. It was not eurocentric or neo-colonial in intention.

question: The Brussel conference in 1889/90 was based on______

option.a: putting an end to slave trade
option.c: furthering the decision on colonialism as previously discussed in the Berlin conference
option.d: deciding on how to penetrate Africa for economic adventurism

solution: The Brussels Conference of 1889/90 was based on putting an end to the slave trade. European powers met to agree on measures against slavery and the slave trade in Africa. The scramble for Africa was handled at the Berlin Conference of 1884/85.

question: According to Lewis Samuel, '________ is identified with pure conquest and unequivocal exploitation...'
solution: According to Lewis Samuel, regressive imperialism is identified with pure conquest and unequivocal exploitation. It is the form of imperialism that takes over a territory only to exploit its people and resources. Progressive imperialism, by contrast, claims to bring development.

question: One of the major defects of the Nigerian council which necessitated its replacement was that....

option.a: the meetings of the council were poorly attended
option.b: the council could only make law for the southern protectorate
option.c: the executive council was powerful than it

solution: One major defect of the Nigerian Council that led to its replacement was that the council was unrepresentative. Most of its members were appointed officials, and only a few Nigerians sat on it. It was advisory and did not reflect the people.

question: An important provision of the 1946 constitution was that it ........

option.c: introduced official majority in the legislative council for the 1st time
option.d: for the 1st time, introduced the office of the head of government at the regional level

solution: An important provision of the 1946 Constitution was that it conceived federalism for Nigeria. It divided the country into three regions with their own legislatures, laying the foundation of a federal system. Full federalism came with the Lyttelton Constitution of 1954.

question: In the all-Nigerian constitutional conference of 1950________

option.a: all official members of the legislative council participated
option.b: it was resolved that the Nigerians federation be organized on ethnic basis
option.c: it was concluded that a quasi-federal structure should be developed for colonial Nigeria
option.d: all unofficial members of the legislative council participated

solution: At the all-Nigerian constitutional conference of 1950, all unofficial members of the legislative council participated. The conference brought Nigerian representatives together to discuss constitutional reform. Official members were colonial officials, not the elected Nigerian representatives.

question: Implementations of the target programmes of the government is the primary duty of the _____ a part of the _____
solution: Implementation of the target programmes of government is the primary duty of the civil service, which is a part of the public service. Civil servants carry out policies and deliver services, while the wider public service includes other government employees. Courts and ministers do not implement programmes in this sense.

question: The most recent target plans and agenda of the United Nations are known as the______
solution: The most recent target plans and agenda of the United Nations are the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). They replaced the Millennium Development Goals in 2015 and aim to end poverty, protect the planet and ensure prosperity by 2030. Agenda 2063 is an African Union plan.

question: The federal judge under the 1963 constitution could be removed by the______
solution: Under the 1963 Constitution, a federal judge could be removed by a two-thirds majority of the National Assembly. This protected judges from arbitrary removal by the executive. The Judicial Service Commission only advised on appointments and discipline.

question: Under the 1999 constitution, the Chief Law Officer and the Supreme Court Judge respectively are the_______

option.d: Chief Registrar of the Supreme Court, Chief Justice

solution: Under the 1999 Constitution, the Chief Law Officer is the Attorney-General and the head of the Supreme Court is the Chief Justice. The Attorney-General is the chief legal adviser to the government, while the Chief Justice heads the judiciary. A Chief Judge heads a state high court, not the Supreme Court.

question: Which of the following was not responsible for the coalition between A. G and N. C. N. C.?

option.b: Awolowo's faction seeking to get N. P. C. out of power as opposed to Akintola's option
option.c: contest for the federal election of 1964
option.d: Akintola's faction which broke out of A. G. to form UPP

solution: The Kano riot of 1953 was not responsible for the coalition between the Action Group and the NCNC. The coalition was formed for the 1954 federal election and later broke up over the 1959 election. The other options describe the real political disagreements behind the alliance.

question: In the 4th republic, the political parties were______
solution: In the Fourth Republic, the political parties were PDP, APP and AD. The Peoples Democratic Party, the All Peoples Party and the Alliance for Democracy were registered for the 1999 elections. APGA came later, and UPGA and NNA belonged to the First Republic.

question: The Economic and Financials Crime Commission (EFCC) scope and nature of duty may not extend to_______

option.a: arresting suspects of cyber crime and online fraud
option.b: arresting the giver and the taker in a corruption case
option.c: conducting trials and punishing persons involved in corruption matters
option.d: investigating cases of substance and drug abuse intersecting with money laundering

solution: The EFCC's scope and nature of duty may not extend to conducting trials and punishing persons involved in corruption. The EFCC investigates and prosecutes suspects, but only the courts can try and punish them. Arresting suspects and investigating fraud are within its powers.

question: The Green Revolution programme was the effected manifesto of the ........ in 1979
solution: The Green Revolution programme was the manifesto of the NPN in 1979. The National Party of Nigeria promised to boost food production and agriculture. The UPN, NPP and GNPP had other programmes.

question: Nigeria's federalism is often considered a flaw along the standard test of the Classical federalism ideology labelled along with_______
solution: Nigeria's federalism is often judged against the classical federal ideology of K.C. Wheare. He defined federalism as a system where the general and regional governments are each independent and co-ordinate within their own spheres. Lincoln, Hobbes and Aristotle wrote about other ideas.
category: Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism

question: The most representative organ of the united nations is the_______
solution: The most representative organ of the United Nations is the General Assembly. Every member state has one vote there, so it represents all members equally. The Security Council has fewer members, and the ICJ settles legal disputes.

question: Executive Council of the African Union makes decision by_______

option.d: the veto of the General Secretariat

solution: The Executive Council of the African Union makes decisions by consensus. Members discuss until they reach general agreement rather than simply outvoting one another. A one-third majority, discretion or a veto by the Secretariat is not how it decides.

question: Amendment of the U. N. O. charter is the duty of the ........
solution: Amendment of the United Nations Charter is the duty of the General Assembly. It considers and approves amendments, which then need ratification by member states. The Security Council and Secretariat have other roles.

question: The fact that the office of the Chairman is rotational in ECOWAS makes it a perfect example of a/an ........
solution: The fact that the office of the Chairman of ECOWAS is rotational makes it a perfect example of a collegiate arrangement. Leadership is shared in turn among member states rather than held permanently by one. A cartel is an economic grouping, and a confederacy is a loose union of states.
